LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction as Jacksonville heads to Baltimore to open Week 9 Imagn Images In the Week 9 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Jacksonville Jaguars . Baltimore is coming off a devastating loss to the Buffalo Bills in which Lamar Jackson returned from his ankle injury and was promptly injured on his first play of the game. The Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley during the contest, and they are now decimated on offense as they head into Thursday night's game. Jacksonville came off its bye last week and laid the smack down on the division rival Indianapolis Colts , winning 42-7 to improve to 5-2 on the season and further solidify their hold on the AFC South. Trevor Lawrence and the offense are rolling, and the defense has been largely excellent so far this year. Will the Jaguars take care of business on the road, or will the Ravens pull off a shocking upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Ravens vs. Jaguars live Date: Thursday, Nov. 5 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Jaguars -9.5, O/U 39.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Jaguars have the ball The Jags enter this game having destroyed the Colts last week behind a monster performance from their running game. Bhayshul Tuten ran 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown, while Chris Rodriguez carried it six times for 41 yards and another score. Rodriguez was limited in practice this week with a hand injury but will play on Thursday night. Tuten's status is up in the air after he didn't practice all week due to an ankle injury sustained against Indianapolis. He played through that injury for the rest of the game, but Jacksonville might choose to rest him here. He's a game-time decision. The Ravens are allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season, with a mere 0.8 of those yards coming before contact, according to Tru Media. Jacksonville could have some issues running the ball, especially if Tuten is out, if the Baltimore front can hold up as it has for most of the season. The Ravens did get clocked for 146 yards on the ground this past week by the Bills, but James Cook averaged south of 4.0 yards per carry. A lot of the damage was done by Ray Davis late in the game with six carries for 30 yards. Josh Allen also chipped in 30 of his own. Trevor Lawrence obviously isn't as mobile or as involved in the run game as Allen, but he can move, and if the Ravens get out of their rushing lanes, he can make things happen as a scrambler. Lawrence has played extremely well so far this season, completing 65.7% of his passes at an average of 8.5 yards per attempt, with 17 touchdowns (and a league-high 8.6% touchdown rate) against just four interceptions. Lawrence's top target is clearly Parker Washington , who splits his time fairly evenly between lining up out wide and in the slot. The Ravens are 21st in net yards per attempt allowed this season, and their cornerbacks ( Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins ) largely haven't played up to expectations. Kyle Hamilton remains excellent against both the run and pass in the slot, so one could expect Washington's route split to lean more heavily toward the outside. Jacksonville may lean toward putting him where he can line up against Humphrey, whose struggles this season have been fairly well documented. Elsewhere on the perimeter, Jakobi Meyers and, to a lesser extent, Brian Thomas Jr . and Josh Cameron are involved. Meyers and Thomas have only combined for three more targets than Washington has, though, so they are more clearly ancillary pieces in the passing game. The box-score expectations for them should be somewhat muted, but they can pop up at any time for key plays. (Thomas did score last week in his return to the full-time WR3 role, for example.) The Ravens, meanwhile, have been relatively stingy against tight ends in the passing game, allowing only 35 receptions to players at the position, so it's probably not going to be the biggest night for Brenton Strange . Tight ends do have six touchdowns against the Ravens, though, so it might be worth it to at least watch out for Strange in the red zone. When the Ravens have the ball You can throw out all of the Ravens' offensive stats. Not only is Lamar Jackson out, but so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. Jacoby Brissett is reportedly on the way to help, but he won't be active on Thursday night. Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano entered the game in relief of Jackson and Huntley last Sunday and will make the start on Thursday night. Fagnano, an undrafted free agent out of UConn, went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception against the Bills. He threw most of his passes to the running backs and did not connect with Zay Flowers even once. Expect the Ravens to lean heavily on Derrick Henry and the run game, but do not expect them to find much success. Henry has been struggling of late to begin with (45 carries for 156 yards and a touchdown over the last three games combined), and the Jaguars have allowed 3.4 yards per carry this season — the single-best mark in all of football. Unless Fagnano and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle pull off some kind of magic act, the Ravens are likely not going to be able to move the ball much on Thursday night. The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Now Playing Share Share Video Does Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore have any chance in 'TNF' matchup? LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. away.headline: Jaguars Injury Report: Vega Ioane set to return for Ravens on Thursday night
away.blurb: Jaguars Injury Report: Vega Ioane set to return for Ravens on Thursday night Share Advertisement Vega Ioane is set to play Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars after missing one game with a knee injury, a boost for the Ravens on a short week. He had no designation on Wednesday's final injury report and was a full practice participant on two days this week. That matters now because the Ravens are trying to steady an offense that has been reworked and is still trying to gel again. Ioane said Monday, “I feel really good. I am confident in my ability to be able to come out,” and Wednesday’s report backed that up with a clean status heading into Thursday night. The rest of the Jaguars injury report is less clean. Nate Wiggins missed Wednesday’s practice because of illness and is questionable, while Jaylinn Hawkins will miss a third straight game because of a knee injury. Bhayshul Tuten has not practiced all week because of ankle and foot injuries and may be a game-time decision, and Travon Walker is also questionable with a rib injury. There is still a gap in the Ravens’ defensive outlook. Wiggins’ status is unsettled, and that leaves one more decision to watch before kickoff for a team already dealing with absences and rotating pieces around Joe Fagnano, Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis on the depth chart. The Ravens elevated Jake Moody and Adisa Isaac from the practice squad for Thursday’s game, a sign that they are preparing for a layered night rather than a simple return. Now the focus shifts to whether the Ravens can use Ioane’s return to their advantage against a Jaguars team that is 5-2, has the NFL’s highest point differential this season and has won 13 of its last 15 regular-season games. Baltimore is 4-4 and trying to snap a three-game losing streak against Jacksonville. For Ioane, the next proof comes under the lights on Thursday night. That is about as clean a return as a team can hope for in the middle of a bruising stretch. There is also the broader picture. The Ravens’ offensive line has been trying to settle after being reworked, and every available body matters when the group is still trying to find rhythm. Nate Wiggins missed practice on Wednesday because of illness and was listed as questionable for Thursday night, adding another little layer of uncertainty to a game that already has enough of them. On a team that is juggling injuries, line changes and a difficult opponent, getting one rookie guard back healthy is not a luxury. It is a necessity. If Baltimore can win this game, it may not be because everything is fixed. It may simply be because enough of the right pieces were available at the right time. away.source: The Sunday Guardian Live on MSN
away.blurb: India, Nov. 6 -- The Baltimore Ravens suffered another major setback during their Week 9 clash against the Jacksonville Jaguars, with safety Kyle Hamilton forced to leave the game due to a hip injury. Hamilton picked up the issue in the second quarter and briefly returned to the field after halftime. However, his discomfort proved significant enough to keep him out for the remainder of Thursday night's contest, with the Ravens officially ruling him out towards the end of the third quarter. Kyle Hamilton Injury Update: Ravens Safety Ruled Out Against Jaguars With Hip Injury The Baltimore Ravens confirmed Kyle Hamilton's exit from Thursday night's game through their official social media account, with several reporters also sharing the injury update. The All-Pro safety was taken to the medical tent for evaluation after picking up a hip issue and initially attempted to return to the field. However, despite briefly playing after halftime, Hamilton was eventually ruled out near the end of the third quarter. The full extent of the injury remains unclear, and the Ravens are expected to provide further updates after the game. Hamilton's absence is a considerable blow to Baltimore's defense, particularly with star quarterback Lamar Jackson already sidelined. As one of the Ravens' most important defensive players, the All-Pro safety plays a key role in limiting opposition offenses. His absence leaves Baltimore with another challenge against Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars, who will look to take advantage of the defensive disruption. Hamilton's absence creates another problem for Baltimore's secondary, which was already without starting safety Jaylinn Hawkins due to a knee injury. The 25-year-old is one of the most versatile players in the Ravens' defense, capable of operating as a deep safety, covering tight ends and running backs, moving closer to the line of scrimmage and contributing as a blitzer. His ability to perform different roles gives the coaching staff flexibility when adjusting defensive formations and coverage schemes. The timing of the injury is particularly concerning with Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence leading the opposing offense. Hamilton's presence is valuable in handling different coverage assignments and limiting big plays through the air. Without him and Hawkins, Baltimore will have fewer experienced options in the secondary, potentially making it difficult to contain Jacksonville's passing attack. Keyon Martin could see an increased role following Hamilton's departure. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. home.headline: Desperate Baltimore Ravens seal huge NFL quarterback trade after Jackson and Huntley injuries
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens have found a fix to their quarterback injury woes by trading for Arizona Cardinals star Jacoby Brissett. The Ravens are down to third-choice undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano ahead of Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , leaving general manager Eric DaCosta desperately scrabbling around for a long-term solution. NFL insider Ian Rapoport was the first to report on Wednesday that the Ravens are now finalizing a trade for Brissett, with the deal set to be completed over the weekend. Fagnano will therefore be on the field for Baltimore on Thursday night, before Brissett takes the quarterback reins in Week 10 for the Monday Night Football showdown against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett had become a prime trade candidate in Arizona after being benched midgame against the Dallas Cowboys and then dropped to QB3 on the depth chart. He started the first eight games of the season for Arizona this season, going 3-5 with a 63.3% pass completion. After Brissett was benched during the loss to the Cowboys, the starting job was handed to Gardner Minshew, with Carson Beck the backup. West Palm Beach native Brissett will join his seventh NFL team in Baltimore, in his 11th season in the league. He was first selected by the New England Patriots in the third round of the 2016 Draft, going on to win the Super Bowl as Tom Brady's backup in his first season. He was traded to the Colts after his rookie season and was the starter there in 2017 and 2019, before alternating as a back-up and starter in Miami, Cleveland, Washington and back in New England, before eventually landing in Arizona. In March 2025 he signed a two-year, $12.5 million deal with the Cardinals and played in 14 games last season. Despite reworking his contract to increase his compensation for the 2026 season, he will become a free agent at the end of the campaign, unless he agrees new terms in Baltimore.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow. The Atlanta Falcons trade the rain for Spain in Week 9 as they travel to Madrid for a matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals at Estadio Santiago Bernabéu. Atlanta suffered a water-logged loss in Tampa Bay on Sunday, lugging a 1-3 slide across the pond to face a red-hot Cincinnati squad opening as a 3.5-point neutral-site favorite Sunday. My Bengals vs. Falcons predictions compare the contrast in current form against the NFL markets, giving you my early leans and NFL picks for this international showcase on November 8. Bengals vs Falcons predictions For help understanding Kalshi probabilities, see our odds calculator . Bengals moneyline Percentages courtesy of Kalshi , one of the best prediction market apps . Early Bengals vs Falcons spread pick: Bengals moneyline The Cincinnati Bengals are laying 3.5 points in Madrid, and even with their current success, I'm avoiding the half-point hook and just taking the Cincy to win outright on Sunday morning. This offense is clicking, especially the passing game. The Bengals have scored 30+ points in three straight games , owning the top EPA per play rating since Week 5 by a large margin (0.216 vs. 0.163 New England at No. 2). Granted, two-thirds of those results have come against the likes of Miami and Tennessee, along with a bye in Week 6. The Atlanta Falcons are coming off a strange game in Tampa Bay. Hard rain influenced the outcome and helped prompt four Falcons' interceptions against a very strong Bucs defense. I'm not putting too much stock in that 16-0 loss. Cincinnati's defense isn't as stout and has given up gains and points to offenses far weaker than the Falcons. I see the Bengals winning, but that extra hook on the FG has me leaning moneyline. Cincinnati and Atlanta will do battle in Spain in a game that could deliver plenty of fireworks for fans. The NFL sent two incredible offensive teams to Madrid that could put up plenty of points. After all, exciting games like this one can really expand the league's footprint on the international stage. Both teams have quite a lot in common. They are both in extremely tight division races where just one win could propel them into first place. However, the difference between the AFC North and the NFC South is absolutely massive. Still, the Falcons have looked impressive at times throughout the season. Meanwhile, the Bengals have been fairly consistent now that their defense is finally looking solid. Though they did not look good against the Titans last week. Regardless, both teams are hungry for a win and have all the offensive weapons needed to get it done. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? And will this game become an offensive shootout or a defensive struggle? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this huge international clash between the Bengals and Falcons in Madrid. Joe Burrow has a repeat of his Week 8 offensive explosion against the Falcons Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports The Bengals looked like a vintage version of the team in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Yes, Cincinnati did get the win. But it was shocking how much they needed to lean on Burrow to get the job done. Fortunately, Burrow is one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL and passed that tough test with flying colors. Burrow finished 38-of-48 for 462 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions. He also had one rushing touchdown. The veteran quarterback simply put the team on his back and willed them to victory. Now Burrow and friends must face an average Falcons defense that's allowed 223.4 passing yards per game this season. Keep in mind that the best opponent Atlanta has faced this season is Chicago. In that game, Caleb Williams shredded their secondary for 305 passing yards. Beyond that game, the Falcons have not been tested very much through the air this season. So just how much damage could Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins do against the Falcons? Burrow will have a repeat performance from last week, going over 400 passing yards and throwing at least three touchdown passes. Cincinnati has to throw the ball to win right now, so they'll be comfortable going guns blazing. To make this even bolder, both Higgins and Chase will each go over 100 receiving yards and score a touchdown. Bijan Robinson will have twice as many rushing yards as the Bengals The disparity between Atlanta and Cincinnati's running game is absolutely massive. Cincinnati has one of the worst rushing attacks in the entire league. In fact, they only average 80.3 rushing yards per game so far this season. That average is quite concerning since they've already played in seven games, so a few bad performances aren't dragging it down. Chase Brown and company just aren't getting the job done. Atlanta is the exact opposite, with their Bijan Robinson-led rushing attack as one of the best in the NFL. They've averaged 134.8 rushing yards per game this year. Only the Buccaneers, Bears, and Bills have a better average. Robinson is the main reason why the Falcons have such a huge advantage on the ground. Just how good will he do in comparison to the Bengals in Madrid? Bijan is averaging 100.6 rushing yards per game in 2026. He is single-handedly outperforming the Bengals on the ground despite failing to break 100 rushing yards in four consecutive games. The Falcons know that they need Robinson to pop off if they want a chance to win this game. They'll design a game plan to do exactly that, and it has a great chance to work. Bijan won't just have more rushing yards than the Bengals, he'll double them up. All it would take is an elite game by Robinson and a pass-happy attack from Cincinnati's offense. Falcons, Bengals combine for at least 80 points in an exciting shootout in Madrid Image Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images This game has all the necessary ingredients of an offensive shootout. Burrow and friends should have no problem scoring at will in this game. Bijan and the Falcons have a huge advantage running the ball. That should keep their offense consistent throughout this game, even if the Bengals start running up the score. Make no mistake, the Bengals have a solid defense that is both frisky and opportunistic. They won't be playing to their strengths when going up against Bijan on the ground. But once the offense gets established, Cincinnati could start to pull away. They should come away with the victory as long as nothing too fluky happens. The Bengals will come out on top thanks to their high-powered offense than can score at the drop of a hat. If they need points late in this game, they will make it happen. The same is not true for the Falcons. Related: NFL picks, predictions, odds for Week 9: Can home dogs bite? Related: NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 2026 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: D/ST

picks.blurb: 3 bold predictions for Bengals-Falcons in Madrid - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means 3 bold predictions for Bengals-Falcons in Madrid (Sam Greene / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn) Keegan Nickoson · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 4, 2026 at 11:24 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cincinnati Bengals landed in Madrid this morning for their overseas game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. Below are some bold predictions for the matchup involving Joe Burrow, Michael Penix Jr. and the current betting markets. Joe Burrow doesn't throw an interception Burrow is coming off a three-interception game against the Titans and is in the midst of an interception-heavy season compared with his first seven games of each season from 2020 to 2026. He threw his most interceptions in a seven-game stretch in 2021, when he threw eight. Funnily enough, he was also throwing a lot of touchdowns, with 17, and completing passes at a high rate (68.9%). That isn't close to his completion percentage this season, as he leads the league at 73%. It seems that when Burrow is throwing interceptions, he's also completing passes and throwing touchdowns . Quite the double-edged sword. Atlanta has a minus-7 turnover differential and doesn't force takeaways often. Look for Burrow to bounce back against the Falcons' league-average defense and play a clean game. Atlanta is held under 13 points As mentioned before, Atlanta turns the ball over a lot. The Falcons are coming off a game in which Michael Penix Jr. threw four interceptions, and he is completing only 61.9% of his passes this season. The most shocking thing about the Falcons' offense is that Bijan Robinson has been held under 100 yards for four straight games, and he hasn't scored a rushing or receiving touchdown in that span. In fact, he hasn't scored a receiving touchdown since Week 1. Drake London, similarly, has struggled, with just one receiving touchdown this season, though he has eclipsed 100 yards twice, including a 9-catch, 194-yard performance in Week 3 against the Green Bay Packers. That was Penix's first game of the season, and it made many think the Falcons had found their stride, but they have since slowed, losing three of their last five. Bengals win by 10 This is basically an amalgamation of the other two predictions. The Falcons' offense is sputtering, and the defense isn't getting enough takeaways to beat a 5-2 Bengals team overseas. The return of pass rusher James Pearce Jr., who had 10.5 sacks in his rookie year, will boost Atlanta. But a motivated Bengals team that wants to prove it is better than last week's overtime win over the Titans will take care of business, covering the 3-point spread by plenty.

away.headline: Falcons Already Rule Out 2 Injured Players For Bengals Game
away.blurb: Falcons Already Rule Out 2 Injured Players For Bengals Game It's rare that a coach will openly rule out players for an upcoming game so early in the week, but that's what Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski did on Monday in his first media appearance of Week 9, in which Atlanta will take on the Cincinnati Bengals . The Falcons have ruled out two players and will spend the week figuring out how to replace them. It also makes sense that that's possible, though, given how early they were ruled out for the week ahead. Branch appeared to be injured during a kickoff return on Sunday. That's where his absence would be felt the most. The Falcons trust him so much as a return man that even after a two-fumble game earlier this season, they stuck with Branch as their returner. The rookie out of Georgia is small, but he's quite explosive, and Atlanta doesn't necessarily have a ready-made replacement for what Branch brings in the return game. Ebukam is out with a hamstring injury. Ebukam has 2.5 sacks on the season so far. He's not necessarily a game-changing pass rusher, but he is reliable, and the Falcons have gotten better contributions out of him this season than they may have expected. Falcons Preparing for Return of 10-Sack Phenom Unlock the latest Heavy on Falcons news — direct to your inbox. The Atlanta Falcons already have some bad injury news on Monday. The Falcons have already determined that both Zachariah Branch and Samson Ebukam will not play against the Bengals. Branch, a rookie wide receiver, and Ebukam, an edge rusher, have both played contributing roles so far this season for Atlanta. Samson Ebukam and Zachariah Branch will miss the Bengals game due to hamstring injuries, and Kevin Stefanski indicated it could be multi-game injuries for either or both. — Josh Kendall (@JoshTheAthletic) November 2, 2026 That last line from The Athletic's beat reporter Josh Kendall is worrisome — that it could be multiple games missed for both players. The small receiver isn't as key on offense, although he could be used in gadget plays and in the screen game, elements that might go away without Branch for a few weeks. That's one of those nagging problems that you never like to see, because it has a tendency to linger longer than anyone wants. Atlanta's pass-rushing depth isn't great to begin with, so moving forward without Ebukam for a little while is not an ideal setup for the Falcons. home.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. home.blurb: Falcons Already Rule Out 2 Injured Players For Bengals Game It's rare that a coach will openly rule out players for an upcoming game so early in the week, but that's what Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski did on Monday in his first media appearance of Week 9, in which Atlanta will take on the Cincinnati Bengals . The Falcons have ruled out two players and will spend the week figuring out how to replace them. It also makes sense that that's possible, though, given how early they were ruled out for the week ahead. Branch appeared to be injured during a kickoff return on Sunday. That's where his absence would be felt the most. The Falcons trust him so much as a return man that even after a two-fumble game earlier this season, they stuck with Branch as their returner. The rookie out of Georgia is small, but he's quite explosive, and Atlanta doesn't necessarily have a ready-made replacement for what Branch brings in the return game. Ebukam is out with a hamstring injury. Ebukam has 2.5 sacks on the season so far. He's not necessarily a game-changing pass rusher, but he is reliable, and the Falcons have gotten better contributions out of him this season than they may have expected. Falcons Preparing for Return of 10-Sack Phenom Unlock the latest Heavy on Falcons news — direct to your inbox. The Atlanta Falcons already have some bad injury news on Monday. The Falcons have already determined that both Zachariah Branch and Samson Ebukam will not play against the Bengals. Branch, a rookie wide receiver, and Ebukam, an edge rusher, have both played contributing roles so far this season for Atlanta. Samson Ebukam and Zachariah Branch will miss the Bengals game due to hamstring injuries, and Kevin Stefanski indicated it could be multi-game injuries for either or both. — Josh Kendall (@JoshTheAthletic) November 2, 2026 That last line from The Athletic's beat reporter Josh Kendall is worrisome — that it could be multiple games missed for both players. The small receiver isn't as key on offense, although he could be used in gadget plays and in the screen game, elements that might go away without Branch for a few weeks. That's one of those nagging problems that you never like to see, because it has a tendency to linger longer than anyone wants. Atlanta's pass-rushing depth isn't great to begin with, so moving forward without Ebukam for a little while is not an ideal setup for the Falcons. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The bigger issues for Indianapolis are on the offensive side of the ball where the Colts average just 20.1 points per game. Yes, it seemed obvious the Colts were waving the white flag following midweek trades of DeForest Buckner and Quentin Nelson but to make sure there was no doubt of their intentions, they endured a smack from Jacksonville on Sunday, 42-7. The Jaguars led 28-0 at halftime and finished with 366 total yards, while the Colts’ offensive woes were on full display turning the ball over three times and amassing a mere 243 yards. Daniel Jones endured a particularly rough afternoon, finishing 19-of-28 for 144 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, including a 92-yard pick-six, before Anthony Richardson replaced him late. Reports Monday indicated that Jones is expected to remain the starter against Dallas, with Richardson staying in the backup role. Sunday’s game is beyond a must-win for Dallas if they are to continue to entertain any hopes of even competing for a playoff spot. The Colts’ offense has been pedestrian on its better days, but the Cowboys have made even bad offenses look elite. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. home.blurb: Cowboys Injury Blow: Malachi Lawrence Out Weeks Before Colts Home Safety Jalen Thompson is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. Schottenheimer said his practice window is not open yet. Wide receiver and returner KaVontae Turpin has been out with a rib injury and missed the Arizona game. Lawrence was the 23rd overall pick out of UCF. He has 13 tackles, 3 quarterback hits, and a sack in eight games, and he took over a starting outside linebacker spot three games ago. On Monday, Schottenheimer said Lawrence’s injury was “a little different” from the other ankle injuries Dallas came out of the game with. FRISCO, Texas — Linebacker Dee Winters was set to do individual work at practice Wednesday, Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said, and tight end Luke Schoonmaker was expected to work back into practice. Rookie outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence is still looking at an absence of a few weeks with the ankle injury he suffered in Sunday’s 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals . Dallas plays at the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, and Schottenheimer said the staff will make decisions after two more days of information. “Get a few guys back rolling along a little bit. Again, Dee Winters, you’ll see him do some individual today. Joey should do good,” Schottenheimer said. “Schooney should be working back into practice. Fergie will be doing some stuff with the trainers. And then both Caleb and PJ are still in the protocol. And then Turp’s still working to continue his rehab. And then Malachi Lawrence is going to probably be a few weeks. So get some more information over the next two days and make a decision.” Winters strained his Achilles in the Oct. 18 loss at the Green Bay Packers and was listed with a calf injury on the injury report. He missed the games against the Philadelphia Eagles and Arizona. Schoonmaker was inactive Sunday with a groin injury after missing practice that week. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. played through an ankle injury Sunday. Dallas acquired him in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier this season. Tight end Jake Ferguson hurt his ankle in the first quarter against Arizona and did not finish the game. Caleb Downs, P.J. Locke Remain In Concussion Protocol Safety Caleb Downs , the 11th overall pick in April, left Sunday’s game in the fourth quarter. Safety P.J. Locke played Sunday for the first time since coming off injured reserve, after missing five games with a foot injury. Downs leads the Cowboys with 30 tackles. The Cowboys’ active outside linebackers without Lawrence are Rashan Gary , Donovan Ezeiruaku , James Houston , Von Miller , and Tyrus Wheat . Dallas sacked Arizona quarterbacks 5 times Sunday, 2 of them by defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . The Cowboys are giving up 152.8 rushing yards per game, and Arizona ran for 202 on Sunday.

Only the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans won’t play in Week 9, giving bettors and fantasy players plenty of options to choose from in Survivor – if you’ve made it this far. In Week 8, the Dallas Cowboys were the one team that really hurt Survivor players, as they lost as a touchdown favorite at home against a frisky Arizona Cardinals team. Unfortunately for the SI Betting team, Dallas was one of the two teams that we gave out for last week's picks. NFL Week 8 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Dallas Cowboys (L) On the bright side for the team, the Cincinnati Bengals held on in overtime to beat the Tennessee Titans, avoiding an 0-2 week when it comes to these picks. MacMillan is getting the chance to buy back in so we can offer some differing opinions in Week 9 and upsets across the NFL in the last few weeks have decimated many Survivor Pools. In Week 9, our team is looking to two teams that are favored by six or more points, including Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs after a tough loss at the hands of the Denver Broncos in Week 8. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 9 Survivor Pool Picks Kansas City Chiefs The Kansas City Chiefs have some issues finishing drives when they take on the elite teams in the NFL, but based on their running game and defense alone, they're well-suited to crush inferior teams. They'll host the New York Jets in Week 9, who can't beat the likes of the Miami Dolphins or Las Vegas Raiders. The Jets' defense has been especially bad this season, ranking 24th in opponent success rate. It's also worth noting that Kansas City doesn't have many more games this season that will make sense for Survivor. A home game against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11 is the other option, but at this point, I believe in the Jets a lot less than Arizona. The Chiefs may not be as explosive as they once were, but on their home field they'll cruise past the Jets and help us advance our survivor entries to Week 10. – Iain MacMillan Dallas Cowboys I know the Dallas Cowboys and their terrible defense absolutely crushed Survivor Players (including our own Iain MacMillan) in Week 8, but I’m willing to go back to them on the road in a must-win game against the Indianapolis Colts. Indy was blown out by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8 – 42-7 – and it’s a candidate to move on from more pieces ahead of the trade deadline. The Colts haven’t been a competitive team for most of this season, starting with a 2-6 record while ranking 29th in EPA/Play on offense and 23rd in EPA/Play on defense. The Dallas defense can’t stop anyone, ranking 32nd in EPA/Play and 30th in yards per play allowed, but this offense is still elite. The Cowboys put up 30 points once again in Week 8 against Arizona, and they’re a top-10 team in EPA/Play and success rate on that side of the ball. Dak Prescott should be able to move the ball pretty easily against a Colts defense that couldn’t slow down Trevor Lawrence (three passing scores) and the Jaguars in Week 8. Indy is an easy team to fade the rest of the season with Daniel Jones clearly in over his head at quarterback. Jones has five touchdown passes, nine picks and has only completed 60.4 percent of his passes. If Dallas can’t win this game, the NFC East crown may truly be out of reach. I’ll take the Cowboys – who are six-point road favorites – to bounce back on Sunday. – Peter Dewey Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Uzomah #87 of the New York Jets hauls in a touchdown against Justin Reid #20 of the Kansas City Chiefs at MetLife Stadium on October 01, 2023 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Chiefs defeated the Jets 23-20. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells · SB Nation Mon, November 2, 2026 at 4:57 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets lost their third straight game and sixth of their last seven on Sunday. Last week the Jets lost at home against the previously winless Miami Dolphins. This week the Las Vegas Raiders broke their own four game losing streak by out-scoring the Jets in a wild 38 – 33 shootout in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Jets took a nine point lead into the locker room at halftime, only to unravel in the second half. The Jets defense was helpless to stop the Raiders attack in the second half as the Jets were out-scored 24 – 10 to close the game. It was a humiliating performance by a putrid Jets defense. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-6 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Any hopes of a playoff run are all but gone. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets go on the road to face the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs in Kansas City next Sunday. The Chiefs have lost two straight games to tough opponents on the road. This week the Denver Broncos barely survived as the Chiefs were stopped on the one yard line as they were trying for a game winning score as time ran out. The Chiefs opened the 2026 season with a dominant 31 – 10 victory over the Denver Broncos. They followed that impressive win with four straight victories over some of the worst teams in the NFL – the Indianapolis Colts, Miami Dolphins, Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Chargers. The 5-0 start to the season was great, but with four of the wins coming against bad teams, it is tough to say just how good the Chiefs are. Now they have lost two straight to tough opponents. Are the Chiefs a top team? Maybe. It's not entirely clear. What is crystal clear is the Chiefs are a far, far better team than the Jets. Teams like the Dolphins and the Raiders have snapped their losing streaks against the Jets in East Rutherford. It seems all but inevitable Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will do the same at home. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Chiefs will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 9.5 points. The game has an over/under of 46.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Chiefs are -520. Chiefs team that is looking to halt a skid of its own. The Jets have lost three straight. They are 2-6 overall (1-3 on the road) and approaching the cellar in the AFC East. The Chiefs are 3-0 at home and 5-2 overall but have lost two in a row and sit in second in the AFC West a ½ game behind the Broncos. The Jets are coming off a frustrating 38-33 home loss to the Raiders in which they produced plenty of offense but couldn’t stop Vegas late. New York scored on its first six possessions, led 23-14 at halftime and 30-21 during the third quarter, but Las Vegas rallied with back-to-back touchdown drives to take a lead late. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, while Braelon Allen rushed for a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown and Adonai Mitchell produced a career-best 142 receiving yards with a score. A big red flag for the Jets continues to be their inefficiency in the red zone on offense and defense: New York went just 2-for-6 in the red zone while Las Vegas finished 4-for-4. Kansas City also melted late in their game last Sunday against the Broncos, blowing a 24-13 fourth-quarter lead in a 28-24 loss at Denver. Patrick Mahomes played much better than he had in the Chiefs’ previous defeat at Seattle, completing 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, including a 73-yard touchdown to Emmett Johnson . Denver, however, scored 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal, and after Mahomes drove the Chiefs inside the Broncos’ 5 in the final minute, Denver made a goal-line stand capped by Malcolm Roach’s sack on fourth down. Historically, the matchup has produced some memorable games. The most recent meeting was a few years ago on October 1, 2023, when Kansas City escaped MetLife Stadium with a 23-20 win. The Chiefs raced ahead 17-0 in the first quarter before the Jets rallied to tie the game at 20 behind Zach Wilson , who completed 28 of 39 passes for 245 yards and two touchdowns. Mahomes had an unusually uneven passing night, finishing 18 of 30 for 203 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, but Kansas City retook the lead on Butker’s 26-yard field goal and Mahomes used his legs to help drain the clock late. picks.headline: Chiefs-Jets betting line & game prediction: KC looks to get back on track
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. The Chiefs enter Sunday as 9.5-point favorites against the Jets at Arrowhead. Kansas City seeks to revive its ground game behind Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson. The prediction picks the Chiefs to beat the Jets 24-13 and cover the spread. The Kansas City Chiefs and New York Jets both need a win. Last week, the Chiefs suffered their second straight loss as the Denver Broncos rallied from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to win 28-24. The Jets suffered their third consecutive loss Sunday, falling 38-33 to the Las Vegas Raiders. How to watch Chargers at Chiefs Kickoff: Noon Central Time Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -9.5. Behind the NYJ-KC matchup Although their goals and expectations entering the season were different, Sunday’s Chiefs-Jets game represents a fork in the road for both teams. The Chiefs entered 2026 hoping to rebound from a 6-11 season and return to the Super Bowl conversation, but their loss to Denver has turned simply winning the division into a dogfight. At the same time, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn needs to show tangible progress in his second season — or his tenure in New York could be short-lived. A home matchup against the two-win Jets presents the Chiefs with the classic get-right opportunity. Their best path to doing so lies in reestablishing the ground game. New York is 21st in the league against the run in opponent yards per game (123.6), allowing 4.0 yards per carry. During his first five games, Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker averaged 133 rushing yards per game. Walker rushed for just 105 yards combined in the losses to Seattle and Denver, but he still ranks third in the NFL with 770 rushing yards. Kansas City will also look for ways to involve rookie Emmett Johnson more after his breakout performance of 143 scrimmage yards against the Broncos. “He’s a super-talented player, and he just brings joy,” quarterback Patrick Mahomes said of Johnson. “He has the right mindset, the right energy, and he wants to be great. Obviously, we have Kenneth, and he’s such a special football player — but to have someone that can come in whenever Kenneth’s tired or needs a break at all, and he can bring energy and juice, too, I think that’s a special combination those guys have there.” Mahomes suggested the Chiefs need to find additional touches for Johnson, potentially through an expanded role in the passing game. Johnson’s 73-yard receiving touchdown highlighted Mahomes’ 321-yard, three-touchdown performance in the loss. Kansas City’s passing game also saw a breath of fresh air with wide receiver Rashee Rice’s return to the lineup. Rice caught a team-high seven passes on eight targets for 53 yards and a touchdown against Denver. He also appeared to have the game-winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter before the play was nullified by a false-start penalty . Reestablishing the ground game with Walker and Johnson could create opportunities for Rice, tight end Travis Kelce and wide receiver Xavier Worthy against a veteran Jets secondary that has recorded just one interception this season. Still, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid respects Glenn’s defensive scheme and personnel. “They’ve got some good veteran guys — whether it’s the safeties, the linebackers,” Reid said. “So you’re not going to have things that are botched up. Sometimes, you get coverages that are kind of messed up a little bit and there are holes there. They do a good job of making sure they can adjust to most things and do it accurately. And they’ve got some guys on the front that are good football players, big guys.” A Jets player to watch is rookie pass rusher David Bailey, who missed his team’s Week 8 game because of a groin injury. Bailey leads the Jets with 5.5 sacks, more than a quarter of the team’s 20 sacks this season. Reid said there’s a “good chance” left guard Kingsley Suamataia returns to the starting lineup after being benched for the second time in four games because of a “coach’s decision.” The Chiefs’ short-yardage and goal-to-go woes have been under criticism this week after a loss in Denver could have been different by dialing up a quarterback sneak. Perhaps this is the week Reid adds it back into the playbook at long last. Despite New York’s disappointing season, quarterback Geno Smith has put together his own resurgence, entering Sunday with 1,913 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and just three interceptions. Smith has posted a passer rating above 100 in five of his last six road games, and the Jets have gained 377 and 439 yards of offense in their past two games. Against a quarterback playing so efficiently, the Chiefs will need to generate more pressure than they did against the Broncos. Pro Football Focus credited Kansas City with just five pressures against Denver’s Bo Nix. While wide receiver Garrett Wilson’s status remains in concussion protocol, running back Breece Hall could return after missing five games. In Hall’s absence, Braelon Allen has been a fantastic replacement, recording at least 100 scrimmage yards in the last four consecutive games. Wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, acquired by New York from Indianapolis in the trade that sent Sauce Gardner to the Colts, established a career high with 142 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Raiders. Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane missed Sunday’s game after aggravating his shoulder injury but returned to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday. Delane’s return is more important given Smith has been brilliant at throwing the deep ball, with 565 yards gained on passes of 20-plus air yards. Defensive end George Karlaftis said Wednesday that coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has preached the importance of developing a “killer instinct” after his unit’s forgettable recent fourth quarter. “No matter what the call is, you just got to find a way to finish,” Karlaftis said. “So I think, especially against a divisional opponent, against a great team that Denver is, when you’re up, when you’re leading, no matter what that lead is, you got to find a way to win the game as a defense. “And I know I felt that. I know the guys in the room, players and coaches, really felt that. And I think that’s something we’re going to take with us and harp on for the rest of the season.” Reid confirmed Wednesday that Harrison Butker will remain the Chiefs’ kicker against the Jets despite his 54-yard miss against Denver. Butker had made three extra points and a 45-yard field goal before pushing his final kick wide right. The Chiefs can get back on the right path and build some confidence by handling the Jets. The problems — an inconsistent pass rush, short-yardage struggles and too many penalties — have been glaring. This is a good opponent to fix all three against. Jets-Chiefs game prediction Beyond the Chiefs’ advantages in record, quarterback and overall outlook, I think this matchup gives Kansas City an opportunity to tap back into the offensive identity that worked early in the season — establishing Walker on the ground to open up everything else. Defensively, clean up the penalties and get to the quarterback. We’ve heard plenty about pressures, but Smith has been sacked 23 times this season — tied for second-most in the NFL. If not Sunday against the Jets, then when? The Chiefs use their get-right game to do just that. away.blurb: Running back Breece Hall, edge David Bailey, and edge Joseph Ossai were listed as limited in the Thursday injury report. Hall has missed five games with a quad muscle injury, while Bailey was out for the Las Vegas Raiders game with a groin injury. Ossai has been in and out of the lineup, most recently with an ankle injury. Hall’s return has been eagerly anticipated for several weeks, although big back Braelon Allen has filled in more than capably in his absence. Trade rumors are floating about Hall being dealt before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, but the Jets are adamant that he’s not going anywhere. His return also raises the question of how he will be deployed alongside Allen, although the latter was seen walking gingerly on the sidelines of the Raiders game in the second half. That may factor into how they will be used, although Allen is not on the official injury report. Bailey would be a big help on a depleted Jets defense. Defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat is on injured reserve, leaving Harrison Phillips and Darrell Jackson Jr. as the men in the middle, a slight drop off from Sweat’s massive presence. Phillips has an ankle injury and did not practice on Thursday, not a great sign for his availability in the upcoming game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Backup linebacker Trevin Wallace is also on the injury report with a groin injury. He was listed as limited in the report. Good news is in short supply around the 2-6 New York Jets right now. But there was a bit of green shoots for Gang Green in their Thursday injury report. A bigger concern for the Jets is the absence of wide receiver Garrett Wilson, who is in the NFL concussion protocol. Wilson was injured on the next-to-last play of the Raiders game, but played the final snap. He came in on Monday complaining of symptoms. He will now have to pass the rigid NFL protocols before returning to action. Receivers Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper Jr. and the tight end tandem of Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq will try to fill the breach, but Wilson is a superstar talent that can change a game when properly used. The Jets will need as many of their frontline talents as they can muster against the Chiefs. The NY team is 9.5 underdogs on the road at Arrowhead Stadium, and they will confront a Chiefs team still smarting from a loss to the Denver Broncos.
