home.headline: Chiefs Share Travis Kelce Injury Update Before Jets Game
home.blurb: Travis Kelce and the Kansas City Chiefs couldn't get back on track in Week 8, falling to 5-2 on the 2026 NFL season after a 28-24 loss to Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos in Mile High City. Now the Chiefs will return to Kansas City in Week 9 for their fourth home game of the season, hosting Geno Smith and the New York Jets. Ahead of the Chiefs' Week 7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, Kelce was listed on the injury report due to an ankle injury. And while he was able to return as a full practice participant ahead of the Week 8 loss to Denver, the Chiefs still had Kelce listed on the injury report with the same ankle issue. Kelce has also remained on the injury report heading into the Week 9 matchup against the Jets. He was initially listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, but the Chiefs upgraded him to a full participant on Thursday, easing concerns about the tight end's status for gameday. Like Kelce, wide receivers Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and Nikko Remegio (hip) were also limited on Wednesday, but were upgraded to full participants on Thursday as well. "Chiefs injury report for Thursday is out," The Kansas City Star's Pete Sweeney wrote on X. "Travis Kelce (ankle), Nikko Remigio (hip) and Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) have been upgraded to FULL participants. Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) remain LIMITED." Mandatory Credit: Eamon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Erik Schlitt · SB Nation Mon, November 2, 2026 at 1:15 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they've strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. "(Dolphins Head) Coach (Jeff) Hafley's done a good job in his first year," Lions coach Dan Campbell said on Wednesday. "A lot of similarities to—just reminds me a little of what we were when we came in. They're young, they're hungry, they're active. They run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball, and they're playing that way." Let's take a closer look at the Dolphins' coaching staff, the scheme they run, and scouting notes from their most recently viewed games. Stadium against the Dolphins (1-6). The NFC North is crowded with the Lions sitting third despite having but two losses. Miami is in the cellar in the AFC East. Lets get the obvious out of the way. The difference between these teams is substantial: Detroit is averaging 29.0 points and an NFL-best 395.4 yards per game, while Miami is averaging only 16.7 points and 290.0 yards. Detroit’s latest victory was arguably its most impressive of the season, a 19-15 win over the previously unbeaten Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field last Sunday. The Lions trailed 7-6 at halftime before Jahmyr Gibbs broke loose for a 30-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Minnesota regained the lead at 15-12 with 8:44 remaining, but Jared Goff responded by directing a seven-play, 69-yard drive and finding Jameson Williams for the go-ahead seven-yard touchdown with 4:35 left. Goff finished 18-of-25 for 176 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Gibbs carried 23 times for 153 yards and a touchdown and Williams caught four passes for 70 yards including the decisive score. The victory came at a cost, however, as linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury and was listed as doubtful on the early Week 9 injury information. The Dolphins are coming off a game that typified their frustrating season, blowing a 13-3 halftime lead in a 24-19 loss to the New England Patriots. Malik Willis and the Miami offense were in control early, but New England erupted for 21 unanswered second-half points, including touchdown passes of 43 and 48 yards from Drake Maye , to turn the game around. Miami finally answered when Willis connected with rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. for a 35-yard touchdown with 2:04 remaining, but the Dolphins failed on the ensuing two-point conversion and New England recovered the onside kick. Willis finished 21-of-32 for 211 yards, two touchdowns and an interception but was sacked five times, while Miami managed only 269 total yards and 74 on the ground. Although the Lions and Dolphins meet infrequently, their most recent games have been surprisingly competitive. Miami leads the all-time regular-season series 8-5, but Detroit won three straight meetings from 2010 through 2018 before Miami answered with a 31-27 victory at Ford Field in 2022. That most recent meeting was an offensive showcase: Tua Tagovailoa threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns, Tyreek Hill piled up 188 receiving yards and the Dolphins rallied from a 27-17 deficit to win, despite Goff throwing for 321 yards. away.blurb: Those tough situations also leave Andrews and every other sideline reporter in a serious bind to carry out their job ethically and accurately. Skip to main content The US Sun US Edition UK Edition Scottish Sun Irish Sun Search Search Sign in My Account The US Sun Video Comment now Next FOX NFL star Erin Andrews has revealed the ‘tough' details behind her coverage of Detroit Lions star Jack Campbell's horror injury. Andrews , 48, was on the sidelines at Ford Field when Campbell suffered a significant neck injury that left him motionless on the turf. home.blurb: Selected No. 27 overall, Johnson played 60 snaps against the Patriots and allowed just one completion for eight yards. PFF listed Efton Chism III as his principal opponent. That limited receiving production is the encouraging part of his Week 8 evaluation. The concern came closer to the line of scrimmage. Johnson missed a tackle and lost contain on another play, although an offensive penalty wiped out the latter. PFF assigned him a 37.5 run-defense grade, contributing to a 56.5 overall grade for the game. His overall rookie grade stands at 64.6, with a listed positional rank of fifth out of 11. That season-long mark provides context for a mixed afternoon: the coverage offered encouragement, even as the run-defense mistakes left clear work to do. Proctor, Miami's No. 12 overall selection, took no snaps in Week 8 because he was inactive due to injury. His overall rookie grade remains 64.8, with a listed rank of second out of seven. There is no new game performance to dissect for the rookie guard. The supplied report does not identify the injury or provide a return timetable, so any projection about his availability would go beyond the information provided. The matchup also offered a small-sample look at a first-round rookie on the other sideline. New England tackle Caleb Lomu played five snaps as an extra eligible lineman, with Zach Sieler listed as his principal opponent. Lomu earned a 41.3 game grade and received two negative run-blocking marks across four running plays. That limited workload should not be treated as a broad verdict, but it adds context to the rookie performances in Miami's divisional matchup. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 9 game between the Browns and Saints: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Saints: Shedeur Sanders is in line to start for the Browns with Deshaun Watson, who was playing his best ball since 2020, entering concussion protocol earlier this week. The biggest difference with Sanders under center appears to be his willingness to stretch the field, as his 7.1 air yards per target in 2025 are more than Watson's 6.7 mark through eight games this season. Sanders is also working with a better receivers than he did a year ago with rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion earning big roles in Todd Monken's offense. None of that will ultimately matter if the run game is dormant — as it was last week (34 yards) in Pittsburgh. The Saints' defense has been anything but great against the run, allowing 139.4 rush yards per game (29th in the NFL) and have given up north of 100 yards in all but one game in 2026. But I do see this being a get-right game for the Saints on all fronts fresh off the bye. Changes were made to the run game ( firing run-game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, signing RB Audric Estimé) and the kicking ranks (Charlie Smyth is expected to handle kicking duties after Daniel Carlson's release), and the entire roster got a little healthier. First-round receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice and could be a boon — if he indeed makes his NFL debut — for Tyler Shough opposite Chris Olave. Getting Kelvin Banks Jr. back along an O-line that has struggled to keep Shough clean in the pocket should also benefit Kellen Moore's unit. Sanders can smile all he wants, but the Saints will get the last laugh Sunday. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Browns 20, Saints 17 Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Saints 23, Browns 20 The Browns are quickly regressing to the mean and going into a hostile environment to face a hungry, young team after a bye doesn't bode well. New Orleans will have emphasized the need to execute better at home for both Kellen Moore and Brandon Staley. Tyler Shough gets it done, having more reliable weapons than Deshaun Watson. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Saints 20, Browns 17 Both offenses are struggling. Deshaun Watson has taken a league-high 33 sacks, and the Browns average 97.6 rushing yards per game. New Orleans has been worse on the ground, but a bye week comes at the right time. The Saints are 0-4 S/U this season – and this game is a candidate for a walk-off field goal either way. They will have to beat the 2-5 New Orleans Saints to do that and hopefully gain some ground in the AFC North. This is a winnable game, and to expect the Browns to win is not a bold opinion. If you want some sort of bold prediction, then we have those too. A forecast that goes beyond that of normal expectations, but also stays in the realm of reality. Here are my three bold predictions for the Browns against the Saints. KC Concepcion rushing score The Saints do not have a good run defense (ranked 29th in rushing yards allowed). I expect the Browns to lean heavily into their running game. This would be especially true if backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders is starting. I expect that Concepcion will be very involved in the passing game. I also think the Browns will look for creative ways to get him touches considering how elusive and explosive he is. Don't be surprised if he finds the end zone on an end-around or a backward pass type play. Judkins goes off I won't go as far as to say that Quinshon Judkins will have his best day of the year because I don't think he outdoes what he did versus the Titans. It makes sense to take the ball out of the hands of a backup quarterback and run the ball early and often. Look for a 100-yard day and a score from Judkins. Shough-ing turnovers There is no debate that the Browns defense has been their strength this year. They rank 13th in points allowed per game and 13th in total turnovers forced. I won't go as far as to predict a turnover fiesta this weekend, but I will predict that Saints Quarterback Tyler Shough has at least two in this game. The Browns are currently in third place within the AFC North division, with the team still thinking about a possible playoff run. While the loss to the Steelers was very disappointing for the Browns, the team still has the utmost confidence as it enters the game this week. However, the Browns will likely be playing the game with backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders, with starter Deshaun Watson dealing with a concussion. It remains to be seen if Sanders will be starting the game, but at this point, it's trending toward happening . Sanders did play last season for the Browns, going 3-4 as a starter at the end of the year. As for New Orleans, they will be coming into the game with a record of 2-5 on the season, but the team did have a bye this past week. New Orleans has gone 0-4 at home this year, giving the Browns some extra ammo going into the week. Experts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report predicted how the contest would go this week. Among these picks, only two of the seven chose Cleveland to go on the road to win this week. O'Donnell and Sobleski were the two to choose the Browns to grab the win this week over the Saints. Cleveland's defense has the talent to keep them in this game, but the offense is likely going to have to win it. For the Browns, whoever is under center will be tasked with getting this team back on track. The offense has sputtered over the last few weeks, and this is an area that Cleveland wants to get back going strong. New Orleans can be a sneaky team, even with their lackluster record on the season, with them having beaten the Baltimore Ravens, with a healthy Lamar Jackson at quarterback, and New York Giants this year. The Saints were expected to be better than where they currently are, so the Browns will need to be careful. Kickoff for this game will take place at 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans.

at the Caesars Superdome brings together two teams in very different positions, as the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take the field against the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Cleveland is third in the AFC North but just one game behind the first place Steelers. New Orleans has lost four of their last five games and sit last in the NFC South, but they are also only a game out of first as they return from their bye. The Superdome, however, has not been kind to the Saints who are winless in four home games (0-4). Cleveland, however, is a respectable 2-3 on the road this season. Plenty of positives happening with the Browns this season, but last week’s performance is not one of them. The Steelers thumped Cleveland, 27-6, in Pittsburgh. Cleveland was held without a touchdown for the first time this year, lost two fumbles, rushed for only 34 yards and surrendered eight sacks, while the Steelers piled up 200 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Forced to throw for much of the afternoon, Deshaun Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards without an interception and Harold Fannin Jr. caught 10 passes for 154 yards. New Orleans has not played in a couple weeks, but their last game was also a loss to the Steelers, 16-10, in Paris on Oct. 25. The Saints managed only 18 rushing yards and were shut out in the second half, but quarterback Tyler Shough produced an encouraging performance through the air, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and one interception. It was symptomatic of the season to date: the offense has no balance. Historically, Cleveland leads the all-time series 13-7, but New Orleans has won each of the last three meetings, including the most recent matchup at this same venue on November 17, 2024. That game was tied 14-14 entering the fourth quarter before the Saints exploded for 21 unanswered points to win 35-14. Taysom Hill was the difference-maker, rushing seven times for 138 yards and three touchdowns, including fourth-quarter scoring runs of 33 and 75 yards, while Derek Carr threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns. Jameis Winston threw for 395 yards and two scores for Cleveland, but the Browns failed to turn their yardage into enough points. Two years later, the central question is similar for both clubs: which offense can translate production into touchdowns? Collins’ workload on Friday could be telling. Wide receiver Denzel Boston (calf) and linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) were both limited participants for the second straight day. They should be fine for Sunday’s game barring a setback. The Cleveland Browns’ Thursday practice report included a name the team definitely can’t afford to lose . Potentially complicating matters is that a groin injury is what cut Fannin’s rookie season short in 2025 and forced him to miss just about the entire voluntary portion of the Browns’ offseason program this past spring. The Browns only have one other tight end on their active roster in veteran Blake Whiteheart. Rookie Carsen Ryan was waived by the team on Thursday for the second time this season. away.headline: Saints get major injury boost as Browns face quarterback uncertainty
away.blurb: Sanders started seven games as a rookie in 2025, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. However, he has seen limited action this season, completing just three passes for 2 yards. For New Orleans, Wednesday's biggest development was the return of Banks, who practiced for the first time since undergoing ankle surgery in September . away.headline: Cleveland Browns Officially Release Former 1,000-Yard Weapon
away.blurb: Ryan began his college career at UCLA, where he posted modest numbers across two seasons, then transferred to Utah for a single year of limited production before landing at BYU in 2025. Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing The Cleveland Browns waived tight end Carsen Ryan on Thursday, bringing a brief and unsettled chapter of the rookie’s professional career to a close only one day after promoting him from the practice squad to the active roster, the team announced . Ryan, selected by Cleveland with the 248th overall pick in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft, has spent the season largely on the margins of the roster. The 23-year-old from Orem, Utah, appeared in seven games and contributed almost exclusively on special teams, logging roughly 85 snaps in that capacity while recording just two offensive snaps. He has yet to record a reception as a pro. His path to the league was unconventional. In Provo, he emerged as a reliable option in the passing game, finishing his senior season with 45 receptions for 620 yards and three touchdowns while starting most of the Cougars’ games. Across four years and three programs, he totaled 74 catches for 1,020 yards and seven scores, production that was sufficient to earn him a late-round draft selection. The Browns initially signed him to a four-year rookie contract worth just over $4.8 million that included a signing bonus of roughly $433,000. After making the initial 53-man roster, Ryan was waived in late October to create space when the team activated quarterback Dillon Gabriel from injured reserve. He cleared waivers, returned to the practice squad, was elevated for a game, and was then promoted back to the active roster on Wednesday. Thursday’s waiver reversed that promotion with unusual speed. The timing has drawn notice around the league. Cleveland practiced Thursday with no public indication of an injury to Ryan, and the team’s transaction release made no reference to an injury settlement. With the NFL trade deadline approaching, some observers have speculated that the move could clear a roster spot for an incoming player, though the Browns have not confirmed any such plan. The tight end room remains thin beyond Harold Fannin Jr. and Blake Whiteheart, the two players who remain on the active roster at the position. Because Ryan was waived rather than released with an injury settlement, he is free to sign with any team. Given his recent history of clearing waivers and returning to Cleveland’s practice squad, it remains possible the Browns will attempt to bring him back if he goes unclaimed. For now, the latest transaction simply adds another entry to a rookie season defined more by roster churn than by on-field opportunity. home.blurb: While they might not be out of the divisional race just yet, the Saints really need things to turn around soon, or else this season will end in disappointment. Fortunately, during their bye week, the Saints got some great news on a key injured player. "Saints first-pick Jordyn Tyson could return from the hamstring injury that has sidelined him as early as next week vs. the Browns , per sources," Schefter reports. "But even if it's not then, he is not far away from playing." Rushing him back before the bye would've made no sense, especially for a team that's likely still trying to climb out of the bottom of the NFC. But now, Tyson is closing in on a return to action, which would make for his NFL debut the moment he's active and steps on the field for New Orleans. Of course, there are areas that the team can improve on, but overall, the Giants are in a good spot. New York will be coming into the week with a record of 4-2-1 on the season, coming off a much-needed bye. The Giants are in full control of the NFC East right now , with the rest of the division underperforming this season. And New York has a chance to put on even more distance between them and a rival this week. New York will be traveling to take on the Philadelphia Eagles this week, offering them a chance to take down an NFC East rival. The Eagles have been a mess this season, with the team seeing all sorts of injuries taking place across the roster. Philadelphia will be coming into the game against the Giants with a record of 2-6 on the season, with them having lost six straight games. The Eagles will be without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts for the game, as he's been ruled out for the remainder of the season due to a scary blood clot problem. The Eagles will be starting backup Joe Milton under center, hoping to give the offense a spark this week. Milton is fairly inexperienced in the NFL, and the Giants will look to take advantage of the situation in front of them. Experts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report all made picks for the upcoming game this week. Within this, all seven experts decided to go with the Giants to grab the win on the road against the Eagles. For the Giants to make this prediction come true, they will need to get the running game going strong. This will open up everything else on offense, giving quarterback J.J. McCarthy more to work with. McCarthy has given the offense new life since taking over for Jameis Winston, and he will be looking to keep everything rolling against a strong Eagles defense. The former first-round draft pick has started to play much more smoothly, with the Giants giving him an opportunity to flash his skills. Kickoff for the game between the Giants and Eagles is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET from Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia.

picks.blurb: Eagles-Giants Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 9 enemy - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Eagles-Giants Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 9 enemy PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles sacks Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants during the third quarter in the game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandon Lee Gowton · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 7:19 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Six straight losses for the Philadelphia Eagles. Can the Birds snap the streak against the New York Giants, a division foe they've owned for a long time? In order to preview this Week 9 NFC East matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Big Blue View . The earnest Ed Valentine kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let's take a look at the answers. [For my answers to Ed's questions about the Eagles, stay tuned to BBV .] 1 – The Giants are off to their most encouraging start to a season in a long time. What has John Harbaugh specifically contributed to this team's turnaround? Credibility. That is the first word that comes to mind. He had 15 winning seasons in 18 years in Baltimore, and he didn't have to prove himself to anyone. He has driven the Giants hard and made them believe they have earned the right to win because of what they have done. I think this piece I wrote on Tuesday is instructive. Harbaugh isn't afraid to challenge players or to step on toes to make the Giants better. 2 – J.J. McCarthy's playing time has been limited but he's shown some promise. To what extent is there confidence in him moving forward this season? I don't know that there is confidence. There are, of course, already fans willing to trade Jaxson Dart and run with McCarthy next year. It is way too early for that, though. I think the best word is "excitement." The Giants did not give up on the season when Dart was lost. They went out and traded for McCarthy, which delivered the message they were not throwing in the towel. McCarthy has shown arm talent and mobility in 5 quarters. He gives them more upside than Jameis Winston. His skillset allows them to run the offense the way they designed it for Dart. Can he keep it up? Can he force the Giants into a Dart-McCarthy debate this offseason? I don't know, 3 – Who are the some of the more underrated Giants players this season? Perhaps some for the Eagles to keep an eye out for in this game? That's hard, honestly. Rookie WR Malachi Fields is developing nicely. Bryan Hudson has taken the center job away from John Michael Schmitz. Abdul Carter doesn't have big sack numbers, but he has been hell to block all season. Deonte Banks has been playing well, really well. He looked like a No. 1 shutdown cornerback in Week 7 against Nico Collins of the Texans. 4 – What's the biggest matchup in the Giants' favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? The run defense has been hit and miss. Saquon Barkley hitting the home run still scares me. The Giants are solid against the run, until they aren't. When they aren't, they give up big plays. Other than that, the thing that scares me is that I still think the Eagles defensive front can dominate games. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Giants currently listed as 3-point road favorites (first time they've been favored in Philly since 2009), what's your score prediction? With great trepidation, I will pick the Giants to win. I'm still wrapping my head around the Giants being favored. They were 10.5-point underdogs two weeks ago in Houston. They have not won in Philly since 2013, and I am well aware that bad things always seem to happen to the Giants at the Linc. I have said for year, though, that at some point things have to turn around. I think this is the year they finally do. I will say Giants 24, Eagles 17 .

away.headline: Giants WR Malik Nabers responds to concerns after sudden injury update
away.blurb: Nabers held no injury designation earlier this week and was a full participant on Wednesday. However, he logged a “DNP” designation on Thursday’s injury report. New York Giants superstar wide receiver Malik Nabers sparked some concern regarding his health on Thursday, working with trainers off to the side of the practice field. When asked about his lack of practice participation on Thursday, Nabers pumped the breaks on concerns regarding his status for Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the division-rival Philadelphia Eagles. “I’ll be good,” Nabers told reporters. Nabers has been absolutely stellar through the Giants’ last four games, reeling in 36 catches for 509 yards and two touchdowns over that span. On Thursday, the NFL recognized him as the NFC Offensive Player of the Month for October. Nabers wasted no time developing chemistry with new quarterback JJ McCarthy. In McCarthy’s first start with the Giants in Week 7, Nabers secured seven of his nine targets for 111 yards in an overtime win over the Houston Texans. Fresh off their Week 8 bye, the Giants will kick off against the Eagles at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. away.headline: Giants WR Malik Nabers reveals game status after missing practice
away.blurb: New York Giants star wide receiver Malik Nabers sat out of the team’s latest practice on Thursday due to a knee injury. However, he’s confident it won’t sideline him for the Giants Week 9 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. According to Jordan Raanan of ESPN, Nabers told reporters that he will be good to go for Sunday’s game. It certainly allows for a sigh of relief as the Giants continue to fend off the rest of the NFC East in first place with a 4-2-1 record. The Dallas Cowboys are in second place at 3-5, Washington Commanders in third at 2-4-1 and Eagles in last at 2-6. There’s no overstating how much Nabers means to New York’s offense as he has already racked up 48 receptions for 605 yards and two touchdowns this season. If Nabers were to ever have to miss any time, the Giants wide receiver corps would become a big concern with rookie Malachi Fields and veterans Darnell Mooney, Charlie Jones and Gunner Olszewski next in line. The Giants are already without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the season after he suffered a multi-ligament left knee injury in Week 2, so Nabers has and will continue to play a very big role in elevating the play of whoever is at quarterback. The Giants will issue an official designation for Nabers on Friday, so all eyes will be peeled when that injury report is released. The No. 6 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Nabers has recorded 175 catches for 2,080 yards and 11 touchdowns in his professional career. picks.blurb: Week 10 Preview: Los Angeles Rams vs Washington Commanders - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 10 Preview: Los Angeles Rams vs Washington Commanders | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Sue Levine, Editor Toussaint Fancher · Last Word on Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After taking care of business and handing the Los Angeles Chargers their seventh loss of the season, the Rams will look to do the same against the Washington Commanders. Although the Commanders' 2-4-1 record is far from impressive, they remain a dangerous team that can win on any given Sunday. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn is currently fighting for his job , and injuries have plagued the team throughout a disappointing season. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has missed several games this season after aggravating a previous arm injury, while several other key players have been sidelined for significant periods of time. While they are 2-4-1, the Commanders still have an opportunity to win the weak NFC East. The Commanders just won their second game of the season after defeating the Philadelphia Eagles and currently sit third in the division. This season, the Commanders are 17th in points per game and 26th in points allowed. They have also struggled on third down, converting just 32% of their attempts, while their defense has surrendered too many points. Although the Commanders have been one of the worst teams this season, they have found success running the ball. Led by their dual-threat quarterback, they average 127 rushing yards per game and protect the ball with only three turnovers. The Commanders' biggest weakness lies in their passing defense, which ranks 27th in the league, allowing 243 yards per game and an opponent passer rating of 100.6. The Rams' success largely depends on quarterback Matthew Stafford's ability to effectively move the ball. Stafford is reportedly dealing with soreness in his right arm. He left the locker room after the Chargers game with a bag of ice on his right elbow. This could be a big game for Puka Nacua . Held to only 80 yards in Week 9, Nacua might have over 100 receiving yards this week. The Rams should still find success running the ball, but the overall game will depend on Stafford's effectiveness passing the ball. In a must-win game for the Rams, this news comes at the worst time. But I think it's a real positive that we're starting his clock." Tight end Terrance Ferguson will also return to practice this week after sustaining an ankle sprain against the Denver Broncos in Week 3. McVay said it's likely that they will start his 21-day clock, but want to see how he's feeling. Cornerback Jaylen Watson aggravated his shoulder again and will take things day-to-day. Watson dislocated his right shoulder in Week 4 and missed the following game before he returned. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton It is early to call the Rams’ game in Maryland Sunday against the Commanders an elimination game, but it sure has the feel of one. Los Angeles is 4-4 and outside the playoff picture currently while the Commanders are 2-4-1 and clinging to life only because the NFC East is so bad. Both teams carry a little momentum into the game. Washington takes the field following their most impressive outing of the season last weekend against Philadelphia while the Rams have won their last two games. The Rams’ latest victory was a 24-9 win over the Chargers in which their offense started extremely slowly, failing to record a first down until late in the second quarter and falling behind 9-3 in the process. Kyren Williams’ one-yard touchdown gave Los Angeles a 10-9 halftime lead. Blake Corum then broke off a 23-yard touchdown run and Matthew Stafford hit Puka Nacua for an 18-yard score in the third quarter. Stafford finished 17-of-25 for 157 yards, one touchdown and one interception, Nacua caught 11 passes for 80 yards and a score, and the Rams rushed for 129 yards while their defense intercepted Justin Herbert twice and kept the Chargers out of the end zone. The Commanders are coming off a much-needed 27-10 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, their first win in more than a month. Washington fell behind 10-0 during a penalty-filled first quarter before scoring the game’s final 27 points and shutting Philadelphia out over the final three quarters. Jayden Daniels completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards, a touchdown and no interceptions, connecting with Stefon Diggs for an eight-yard score, while Rachaad White ran 11 times for 55 yards and the clinching touchdown. Washington finished with 135 yards rushing, but its defense was the bigger story, sacking Tanner McKee five times, intercepting him once and limiting Saquon Barkley to just 30 yards on 13 carries. That showing by the Washington defense sets up the primary storyline for Sunday’s game: the Commanders’ resurgent pass rush against Stafford. The other of course relates to Daniels and his ability to attack a banged-up Rams’ secondary. Historically, Washington has had the upper hand in the series, holding a 24-13-1 regular season record against the Rams, but recent meetings have been much more balanced. Washington has split its past four matchups with Los Angeles dating to 2015, and Sunday’s game will be the Rams’ first trip to Washington since 2020, when Los Angeles won 30-10 in the game that marked Alex Smith’s remarkable return to action following multiple leg surgeries and a long rehab. Rams coach Sean McVay spent seven seasons in Washington’s organization and three as its offensive coordinator before taking the Rams’ job. away.headline: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett Returns, But Bad News Continues to Pile Up
away.blurb: While the Los Angeles Rams got some good injury news on Wednesday, the injuries also continue to pile up. Both Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson opened their practice windows as they work to return from injured reserve. However, cornerback Jaylen Watson’s season is over with a shoulder injury and cornerback Trent McDuffie was a non-participant with a back injury. The biggest knock for the Rams is Watson being placed on injured reserve and being out for the season. Watson was the team’s top free agent signing as the Rams looked to rebuild their cornerback room this offseason. After missing Week 4 with a dislocated shoulder, Watson reaggravated the injury in the third quarter of the team’s win against the Chargers. “The likelihood of it coming out and doing further damage to it is a very high probability. You could strap it, but it would restrict his movement,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Just some of the different things that we've received from our doctors, it's the right thing to do by him, even though it sucks because he's been such a bright spot for us.” “It's exciting. It's great to be able to get him back out there,” said McVay. “He'll probably take half the reps today. If you have 30 reps, he'll take 15 and then we'll see how he feels coming out of that. Hopefully, it's just a little bit of an increase incrementally at a time.” In addition to Garrett being back, Ferguson and running back Ronnie Rivers returned to practice as well. Ferguson should provide some insurance if Parkinson can’t play for a second straight week, while Rivers could be helpful on special teams. Also limited were linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), left guard Steve Avila (hamstring), and wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back). Coming out of the Chargers game, one of the big stories was Matthew Stafford being seen walking out of the locker room with ice around his right arm . Stafford showed up as a full participant on Wednesday’s injury report with a right elbow injury. away.headline: Los Angeles Rams Face New Injury Concern With Matthew Stafford
away.blurb: Los Angeles Rams Face New Injury Concern With Matthew Stafford - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' What MLB's labor proposal means Los Angeles Rams Face New Injury Concern With Matthew Stafford The Rams are facing a new injury concern with Matthew Stafford. Getty Josh Buckhalter · HEAVY Tue, November 3, 2026 at 1:57 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay chose to remain mum on Matthew Stafford "Rams QB Matthew Stafford left the locker room yesterday with a bag of ice wrapped to his right [elbow]," the LA Daily News' Adam Grosbard reported on X on November 2. "Sean McVay said he's dealt with some soreness in the arm, but deferred to Stafford on how he's feeling." Stafford, 38, completed 68% of his passes for 157 yards, 1 touchdown, and 1 interception, while absorbing 1 sack in the win over the Los Angeles Chargers . He held his usual postgame presser, but the update creates more questions than answers. Matthew Stafford Injury Concern Amid Rams' 'Tightrope' Act The concerns about Stafford's health are new but not wholly unexpected, and not just because the reigning Most Valuable Player dealt with a back injury before last season and had his 2022 campaign cut short due to a neck injury. Instead, it is because of the burden the Rams have placed on their veteran quarterback amid all of their injuries. "They're asking a 38-year-old Stafford to overcome a lack of trust with young options while fearing the next turnover," The Athletic's Nate Atkins wrote on November 2. "The Rams are walking a tightrope over fire right now. If they stay on the rope, they can still reach the promised land. "But they can't afford to slip anytime soon." The good news is that the Rams have lessened the load on Stafford, who averaged over 53 pass attempts per game from Weeks 3 through 5. He has averaged 29.0 attempts per game in the three games since. The Rams went 1-2 during the former stretch and are currently on a two-game win streak, their first of the 2026 campaign. Their backup situation also remains a source of intrigue. Last season, the Rams could turn to veteran Jimmy Garoppolo if Stafford went down, just as they did during training camp in 2025 and after the star's next injury in that 2022 season. At this point, Rams fans can only hope this situation does not deteriorate into a similar experience. home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. home.headline: Commanders-Rams Injury Report Raises New Concern on Depleted Defensive Line
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders released their first Week 9 injury report as the team gears up for its matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. Jer'Zhan (Johnny) Newton practiced fully on Wednesday after being limited throughout last week. A day after the team placed both starting defensive tackles on injured reserve , Shy Tuttle was limited with a shoulder injury. Newton returned to practice last week as the team opened his 21-day practice window while he recovers from a torn pectoral muscle. He was downgraded to OUT before the Eagles game, but Commanders head coach Dan Quinn likes how his return is progressing. "The arrow is going up for sure, and I'm very optimistic for it. But it's important to stack another good week of him in practice and movements." Newton must still be activated from injured reserve before he can play against Los Angeles. Treylon Burks was another name missing from Wednesday's practice, as the receiver continues dealing with the foot injury that left him questionable against Philadelphia . He played anyway and led Washington with 81 receiving yards on three catches, including a 53-yard gain. With Terry McLaurin out for the season, the Commanders need Burks available, but missing Wednesday's practice doesn't necessarily mean he'll be unavailable against Los Angeles. Stefon Diggs also sat out Wednesday, although his absence was listed as rest rather than an injury. John Bates (shoulder) and Sam Cosmi (knee) were limited, while Jayden Daniels (left elbow) and Colson Yankoff (knee) practiced fully. Thursday's injury report should provide a clearer picture of where Burks and Tuttle stand heading into the weekend. McDuffie did not practice, nor did Colby Parkinson, Kam Curl or Joe Cardona. McDuffie injured his back last week against the Chargers, Parkinson is still dealing with a rib injury and Curl picked up a foot injury. There is some good news, though. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Denver Broncos (6-2) head to Charlotte on Sunday looking to strengthen their hold on first place in the AFC West when they face the Carolina Panthers (3-4) at Bank of America Stadium. Although their record is a game below .500, the Panthers are also a first place team as they sit atop the NFC South. The Broncos have won four straight since a loss in early October at San Francisco. Carolina has suffered lopsided defeats in each of their last two games. This past Sunday, Bo Nix and the Broncos staged an impressive comeback to beat Kansas City, 28-24. Denver trailed 24-13 in the fourth quarter before Nix found Nate Adkins for a touchdown and Jaylen Waddle for the two-point conversion. After a missed Chiefs’ field goal, Nix connected with rookie Jonah Coleman for 51 yards, setting up Coleman’s go-ahead five-yard touchdown with 1:56 remaining. Denver then preserved the victory when its defense stopped Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs on fourth-and-goal. Nix finished 20-of-32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Denver has now won 15 one-score games over the past two seasons. As mentioned, Carolina has lost two straight, most recently losing at Green Bay last Thursday 27-19. The Panthers actually led 10-6 early in the second quarter behind a Chuba Hubbard touchdown, but Green Bay answered with 21 straight points to take control. Bryce Young completed 23 of 41 passes for 209 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Hubbard supplied 81 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries plus seven catches for 38 yards. Carolina made things interesting when Young hit Jalen Coker for a 26-yard touchdown with 5:37 left, but the Panthers failed on the two-point conversion and never scored again. The most troubling stats to emerge from the game was Young being sacked six times and Carolina’s offense managing only 258 yards. The central storyline is therefore strength against vulnerability: a Carolina offensive line that surrendered six sacks at Green Bay now has to protect Young against Denver, while the Panthers must find a way to slow a Broncos team that has developed a remarkable habit of winning tight games. Recent history strongly favors Denver. The Broncos hold a 7-2 all-time advantage over Carolina, including the postseason, and won the teams’ most recent meeting 28-14 in Denver on October 27, 2024. That game featured the same starting quarterbacks expected Sunday: Nix shredded Carolina for 284 yards and three touchdown passes, added a rushing touchdown and posted a 124.2 passer rating, while Young threw for 224 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: S Brandon Jones Trending Toward Inactive
away.source: Denver Broncos On SI on MSN
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: WR Pat Bryant gearing up for return
away.blurb: After missing the last four games with an ankle injury, the Denver Broncos designated wide receiver Pat Bryant to return from injured reserve, opening his window to be activated to the 53-man roster. WR Courtland Sutton, meanwhile, was considered limited as he enjoyed a veteran rest day. Ditto for defensive end Zach Allen. Both will play against the Panthers. What's less certain is the Week 9 status of four key defensive players in safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder), and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) — all of whom did not practice on Wednesday. Jones, Abrams-Draine, and Uwazurike were injured in Week 8 and their status for Sunday's contest is to be determined. They'd need to get in at least a few limited practices on Thursday and Friday to increase their chances of suiting up. Hufanga has been sidelined since Oct. 11 — he was initially expected to miss 2-3 games — and could be held out once more with Denver's Week 10 bye looming. This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/broncos/onsi as Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: WR Pat Bryant Gearing Up for Return . That will likely happen sooner rather than later as Bryant was marked as a full practice participant on the team's first Week 9 injury report ahead of Sunday's road game at Carolina . Bryant was carted off the field amid Denver's Week 4 loss against the 49ers with what appeared to be a significant injury, though the second-year wideout avoided being placed on short-term injured reserve. Also listed as a full participant was Bryant's fellow pass-catcher, WR Jaylen Waddle, who's still nursing a minor chest issue. Waddle looked no worse for wear in last week's comeback victory over Kansas City , snagging three passes for 39 yards and a touchdown. A Potential Boost to Denver's Passing Offense Finally, the Broncos — if they choose to activate him this week — could be back at full strength in their receiving corps, with Waddle, Sutton, Bryant, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin all sharing the same field together. Bryant totaled nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown prior to going down, with his lone score coming in Denver's Week 3 upset of the Los Angeles Rams. He also snagged a two-point conversion earlier in the season. With sure hands and a wide catch radius, Bryant will again provide quarterback Bo Nix a security blanket over the middle of the field and in the red zone, helping to boost a passing offense that currently ranks 25th in the NFL, averaging 180.4 yards per game through the air. home.headline: Could the Panthers make a trade deadline move? 5 potential targets
home.blurb: A plausible case can be made for the Panthers to add reinforcements at the deadline. There's also a reasonable case to trade away an expensive and/or underperforming player, especially if a contender offers a quality draft pick in return. General manager Dan Morgan could also, as he did last year, simply stay put with his roster and hope history repeats itself with the Panthers on top of a forgettable divisional scrum in January. The Panthers have limited salary cap space ($684,323, as of Wednesday, according to the NFLPA salary cap report). But they have the flexibility -- like all NFL teams -- to maneuver their cap situation with contract restructures that would open up space while pushing current cap charges into the future. Still, it's more likely the Panthers look for a bargain (particularly players on rookie deals) than a big name on the trade market. Why Panthers would pass on McDonald: The Panthers have been terrible against the run for years, and that aspect of their defense is a priority for coach Dave Canales and company down the final stretch of 10 games. McDonald won't offer a whole lot in that regard, and it could be argued he is somewhat redundant with Princely Umanmielen already on the roster. McDonald, while he would come cheap this year ($1.66 million base salary), is set to play on a guaranteed $13.7 million fifth-year option in 2027.And because of McDonald's cost-effectiveness, as well as his pass-rushing success, the Jets aren't likely to part ways with him without a substantial return. Why trading Hunt makes sense for the Panthers: Hunt has struggled this season between Fortner and rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling . With Christensen on the mend, perhaps the Panthers could make Hunt available for a notable return. Why Panthers would pass on Hunt trade: The Panthers' offensive line depth is a mess right now. The starting lineup has had its lumps, so it's fair to wonder what Hunt would bring in return, especially as the front office isn't likely to just give him away. While opening up cap space and getting something for Hunt sounds appealing on paper, a team with playoff aspirations probably shouldn't risk moving on from a proven talent in the middle of a postseason push. home.blurb: The Denver Broncos got a bit of a boost to start practice this week with wide receiver Pat Bryant being designated to return from injured reserve . Given Hufanga's situation, I would guess they keep him out this game and just plan to have him make his return after the bye week. home.headline: Both Broncos starting safeties in danger of missing Panthers game after practice injury update
home.blurb: According to the Broncos' official injury report, Hufanga remains sidelined by an ankle injury , while Jones is dealing with a hamstring issue. Neither player has been ruled out, but their availability remains uncertain. Hufanga has missed Denver's last three games since suffering his injury against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Broncos have already needed to make adjustments in the secondary while waiting for his return. Jones, meanwhile, entered the previous matchup against Kansas City with a questionable designation because of his hamstring. His potential absence would leave Denver facing another significant adjustment in the defensive backfield. The injury concerns extend beyond the safety position. Cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury, while defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike sat out because of a shoulder issue. picks.headline: NFL Week 9 odds: Texans open as heavy road favorites vs. Chargers
picks.blurb: Currently sitting at 2-5, the Texans must get back to their winning ways if they plan on making a postseason push. Right now, no one should be talking about the playoffs, especially since Houston has blown three fourth-quarter leads and remains winless at home. The Texans will travel to Los Angeles for a date with the winless Chargers in Week 9. The Bolts, who could be gunning for the No. 1 overall pick, fell short on Sunday in a battle of L.A. showdown against the Rams , where the offense mustered up nine points. The struggles continue for Justin Herbert in a year to forget. While only being sacked twice, the former top gunslinger threw for just 257 yards and threw a pair of interceptions. The Rams' offense could only muster 281 yards, but two touchdown runs from Blake Corum and Kyren Williams was the x-factor. As for Houston, it's coming off the bye week, though the roster could be in question at wide receiver once more. Second-year breakout star Jaylin Noel suffered a turf toe injury during the loss to the New York Giants in Week 7 and will miss the remainder of the regular season. The Texans could also be without starters Jalen Pitre and Reed Blankenship in the secondary, along with running back David Montgomery, who hasn't played in nearly a month. What do oddsmakers think about this battle between the two struggling teams that can't seem to pick up a win to save their season? Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Two of the league’s bigger disappointments meet Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium when the Chargers (0-7) host the Texans (2-5). Los Angeles is the only team in the NFL without a win and are as a result, firmly entrenched in the cellar in the AFC West. Houston sits in second in the AFC South but are three games behind the first place Jaguars. The Texans take the field following their bye week. They were last in action on October 25 when they lost a disappointing 27-21game in overtime at home to the New York Giants. Houston rallied from a seven-point fourth-quarter deficit to force overtime on C.J. Stroud’s 3-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson with 52 seconds remaining. Stroud finished 17-of-28 for a season-low 153 yards and two touchdowns, while Woody Marks ran 19 times for 66 yards, but Houston produced only 237 total yards. The glaring issue was on defense. The Texans surrendered a season-high 188 rushing yards, including 124 and a touchdown to Cam Skattebo . The Chargers’ search for their first victory continues following their most recent game, a 24-9 loss last Sunday to the Rams. The Chargers had a 9-3 lead late in the first half but went scoreless over the final 38 minutes of the game. Justin Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards, but threw two interceptions, and the Chargers failed to reach the end zone for the second consecutive game. Los Angeles managed just 64 yards rushing with all nine Chargers’ points coming on Cameron Dicker field goals. The Chargers hold a narrow 6-5 advantage in the all-time series, but Houston has won the last two meetings, including two especially consequential victories. The Texans routed Los Angeles 32-12 in the AFC Wild Card round following the 2024 season, intercepting Herbert four times as Houston erased an early 6-0 deficit and ran away with the game. Houston then went back to SoFi Stadium in Week 17 last season and beat the Chargers 20-16, giving the Texans consecutive victories in the series for the first time. Ryans described Montgomery's recovery as "week-to-week," while acknowledging that the running back has made progress. Now, that's encouraging news if you're a Texans fan. But let's be real. Progress doesn't move the chains, pick up a blitzing linebacker or punch the football into the end zone on third-and-goal. Montgomery suffered the injury during Houston's Oct. 11 matchup against the Tennessee Titans and has already missed two games. Sunday's absence will make it three straight, leaving Houston with another offensive challenge as the season moves deeper into November. The bigger question isn't simply when Montgomery returns. It's whether the Texans can establish a consistent rushing attack without him. home.headline: Chargers announce injury news on two key players
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: Jim Harbaugh spoke to the media on Wednesday and announced that injured reserve return windows for David Njoku and Denzel Perryman have opened. Njoku is among the handful of players currently on the IR. The veteran tight end has been dealing with a fibula injury, but he can soon be evaluated for a return to the 53-man roster. Njoku has missed the last five games after suffering the injury in Week 2 against the Raiders . However, he could return prior to their Week 9 matchup against the Texans . The Chargers have been hampered by injuries to start the season, but things may be going their way now. As for Perryman, he is also close to returning. Perryman has been dealing with an undisclosed injury and has yet to play this season. He was placed on the IR to start the season. Perryman is in his second stint with the Chargers and his eighth with the team. The Chargers will seek their first win of the season this Sunday. They remain the only winless team in the NFL. Los Angeles Chargers Place Derwin James Jr. on Injured Reserve Skip to main content Primary nav TEAM The Los Angeles Chargers today placed safety Derwin James Jr. , on Reserve/Injured. In a corresponding move, the team signed cornerback Isas Waxter to the active roster. In addition, the Bolts elevated cornerback Kaiir Elam from the practice squad for Sunday's game. Waxter (first name pronounced eye-SAHS) spent the 2025 season on the Los Angeles practice squad after initially signing as an undrafted free agent with Seattle. He has appeared in a pair of games this season for the Bolts as a standard elevation. Waxter appeared in 46 collegiate games over five seasons (2019-24) at Villanova, compiling 108 tackles (75 solo), three interceptions and 19 passes defensed. The Newark, N.J., native added a sack, two tackles for loss, three forced fumbles and a recovery for his career, earning second-team All-Colonial Athletic Association honors in 2023. A four-year NFL veteran, Elam (first name pronounced kai-EER) has started 19-of-43 career regular-season games with Buffalo, Dallas and Tennessee. He entered the NFL as the 23rd overall selection in the 2022 NFL Draft by the Bills, totaling 111 tackles (77 solo), a pair of interceptions, eight pass breakups, four tackles for loss and three fumble recoveries over the course of his career. Elam has appeared in five postseason games, making a start and posting 14 tackles (eight solo), two interceptions and three pass breakups. He saw action in 35 games over three seasons (2019-21) at the University of Florida, registering 79 tackles (52 solo), six interceptions, 26 pass breakups and a fumble recovery. In his sophomore year in 2020, Elam earned first-team All-Southeastern Conference honors and was a semifinalist for the Jim Thorpe Award, which annually recognizes college football's top defensive back, after picking off two passes and recording 13 pass breakups. news

Sunday's absence will make it three straight, leaving Houston with another offensive challenge as the season moves deeper into November. The bigger question isn't simply when Montgomery returns. Without him, Houston loses some of that physical identity. And here's where things get interesting. picks.headline: Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9
picks.blurb: Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 (Rich Storry-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots were able to take down the Miami Dolphins last week, improving their record to 5-3 on the season. New England didn't play the prettiest game on the field, but at this point for them, a win is a win. With all the injuries that the Patriots have seen take place, especially to the offense, the team has been able to stay alive. This week, the Patriots will be hosting the Green Bay Packers, giving the team a real challenge on its hands. Green Bay, like New England, has started to play much better of late, finally put things together on the field. The Packers will be entering the game with a record of 5-3, with both sides of the ball clicking for the team. New England is going to have to be careful in this game; otherwise, they could be on the losing end of the contest. Analysts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report all made picks for the game between the two teams. But six of the seven experts went with Green Bay to take down the Patriots in this matchup. Only Gagnon went with New England to win the game, despite this contest being played at home for the Patriots. But the Packers recent play likely has to do with how confident those around the league are heading into the week. One key for New England this week will be how quarterback Drake Maye performs, especially when it comes to turnovers. The Green Bay defense can be feisty at times, using its opportunistic nature to get the best of opposing quarterbacks. Maye will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that the Patriots have seen this year, going against this tough defense. But the veteran quarterback has done well this year , even with his issues earlier in the season. Against Green Bay, the Patriots may need to rely on the running game a little more, taking some pressure off Maye's shoulders. Head coach Mike Vrabel will have to put his signal-caller into a strong position to win, avoiding any issues. The offensive line will also need to hold up in the game, giving Maye time to throw the ball against this defensive front. Kickoff for the Patriots game against the Packers is scheduled to take place at 1:25 p.m. PT/4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough.

That's when we get to see which erstwhile contender might be for real when the Green Bay Packers face the New England Patriots. Sunday night brings the new-look Chicago Bears against a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that didn't need to complete a single pass last week (OK, a bit of a stretch but should still be fun). And on Monday, Josh Allen takes on the league's best, most aggressive defense. That's made Week 9 a bit easier to predict, but it's not chalk across the board on our end. Welcome back to For The Win's straight-up, moneyline NFL picks column. I ended 2023 as Pickwatch’s top expert in a field of hundreds. The two seasons that followed? Ehhhhh, we don't like to talk about that. But I'm back and hopeful I'll either be good enough to rejoin the top 25 or, barring that, be so destructively bad you're left with no choice but to fade my picks all the way to prosperity. Joining me for 2026 is a six-person panel ranging from FTW editors (Charles Curtis, Wajih AlBaroudi and Jeff Smith) to betting analysts (Prince Grimes) to NFL writers (Robert Zeglinski, who is THRIVING this year, and Andrew Joseph). Here are our Week 9 picks. Jaguars at Ravens Bengals at Falcons Browns at Saints Cowboys at Colts Broncos at Panthers Lions at Dolphins Giants at Eagles Jets at Chiefs Rams at Commanders Texans at Chargers Cardinals at Seahawks Packers at Patriots Raiders at 49ers Buccaneers at Bears Bills at Vikings Season to date: Since our editing software occasionally struggles to make these picks super clear, here they are in an easier to read (but impossible to cut and paste) .jpg you can click to expand: Let's break out three games to talk about. Survivor pick of the week: Houston Texans (-4.5) over the Los Angeles Chargers We haven't burned Houston yet in my quest to turn what should be the easiest pick of the week into a coin flip. Now the Texans are coming off a bye and facing the shattered remnants of the Chargers on a home field that will be even more listless than usual in Los Angeles. DeMeco Ryans has a path from 2-5 to 6-5 over the next four weeks (against the Chargers, Browns , Colts and Ravens). He's not going to collapse on the first step. Last week : 1-0 Season to date : 4-4 Hardest favorite to back: New England Patriots (-3) over the Green Bay Packers Tom Brady returns to Foxborough, which Fox would like you to believe is a momentous occasion but isn't the first time he's been back to Gillette Stadium . The bigger story is two 5-3 teams have stabilized after iffy starts and a Drake Maye-Jordan Love shootout could be the best game of the year. Or, the Patriots' injuries could finally sink them back to "pretender" status. Why I like this pick : The Patriots have only lost once at home in the last 58 weeks (to the Buffalo Bills). Maye has been able to make adjustments on the fly, elevating targets like Eli Raridon, Pop Douglas and Kyle Williams the last few weeks with A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins all missing time due to injury. That includes a comeback effort in Week 8, albeit against a bad Miami Dolphins team. The Packers have the same problem many Matt LaFleur teams have had; they struggle to close out games. The run attack is a disaster. No one trusts Trey Smack with an end-of-half field goal at this point, let alone one that could decide a game in the fourth quarter. Why I don't like this pick : New England has yet to play a game without committing a turnover. Green Bay forces them more than all but one other team in the NFL. That leaves a top 10 defense to clean up a Patriot offense potentially missing its top three wideouts, its 1b running back and both its starting guards. The Patriots defense is solid, but not spectacular. Jordan Love is playing the best football of his life, taking shots downfield with incredible touch and accuracy. Granted, far too many of those throws wind up dropped, but that hasn't deterred him from taking risks capable of paying off in a massive way. Last week : 0-2 Season to date : 6-2 Upset pick of the week: Atlanta Falcons (+3) over the Cincinnati Bengals Last week's upset pick failed to account for a monsoon in Tampa. Still, it was worth it just to see Michael Penix Jr. throw more interceptions than the Buccaneers had pass attempts. AND YET, I AM ON THE FALCONS FOR A SECOND STRAIGHT WEEK. Well, let's unpack just how dumb I am. The Bengals keep touching the stove. Cincinnati just gave up 121 yards and two touchdowns to Tony Pollard and now has to face Bijan Robinson. That defense was the backdrop for the biggest game of Cam Ward's career and now has to face an angry Michael Penix Jr. who goes from rainstorms to the cozy confines of Madrid, which... huh actually I don't know how that's gonna affect things. The Falcons have quietly engineered a borderline top 10 defense and have only allowed 11 passing touchdowns this fall. That will place some of the onus on a run game that's underwhelmed behind the average efforts of Chase Brown. The Bengals' best win this season is over... the Buccaneers? The Lamar Jackson-less Ravens? The Dolphins or Titans? Ooooof, that resume. It's the Falcons. Joe Burrow just racked up about 1,000 yards on his own to fend off the Titans last week. The Cincinnati secondary is capable of shutting down a top-heavy receiving corps. It's the Falcons. picks.headline: Packers at Patriots: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 9 game
picks.blurb: The Patriots are likely to be on A.J. Brown watch once again. After the receiver missed Sunday's win over the Dolphins with a knee injury, Mike Vrabel said Monday that the team would need to see how Brown progresses before determinig his status for the upcoming tilt. Micah Parsons is expected to make his much-anticipated return to practice this week for the Packers, but he might still be a long way out from contributing. Matt LaFleur said the edge rusher might need the full 21-day window before being added to the active roster, which would mean a late November return. If there is any change to running back Josh Jacobs' disciplinary status, it won't come from the Packers. LaFleur said this week that the team plans to continue on with the ball carrier as the NFL extends its investigation. Patriots vs Packers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Patriots -3.5 Moneyline: Patriots -160; Packers +145 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Patriots vs Packers USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Patriots 24, Packers 23 The Patriots are 17-0 with Drake Maye when favored by at least a field goal and we just may close there by Sunday afternoon. Who am I to disagree with a great trend? The Packers possess a dynamic passing offense but, even with Josh Jacobs back, still can't run the football with any efficiency. Plus, Christian Watson is dealing with a rib injury that sent him to the hospital for a portion of last week's primetime win over the Panthers. The Pats have the personnel to take advantage defensively, but Maye's offense also has questions around injuries to A.J. Brown, Hunter Henry and others. I'll take New England at home, but I'm expecting nervous pacing around living rooms throughout Massachusetts before this one is settled. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Packers 28, Patriots 27 Bombs away. With a matchup of two daring downfield passers and lackluster run games, both teams could air it out early and often against one another. Between their reliance on Jordan Love connecting on vertical shots and the pass rush picking up the rest of the defense with pressure, Green Bay might be more reliant of the two on igniting big plays. But the Packers' explosiveness shouldn't be doubted, and it could lead the team to its fifth win in six games. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 26, Patriots 23 Good luck figuring these teams out. At times, Green Bay looks like a bad team. Then it looks like a Super Bowl contender. The same is true of New England, meaning there is a large range of outcomes we could see in Week 9. Will A.J. Brown play for the Patriots? Does it matter? Drop issues have plagued the star receiver and there's no sign of that disappearing anytime soon. On the other side, Christian Watson made 'Thursday Night Football” look like the WWE with his dramatic return. In the end, we'll trust the Packers offense to be the difference. away.blurb: Nixon did not practice on Thursday while dealing with a groin injury. He was listed as limited on Wednesday. The veteran has not missed a game since signing with the Packers before the 2022 season, but he might need to practice Friday to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday against the New England Patriots. Lloyd, who suffered through two injury-plagued seasons to start his NFL career, has his first injury of 2026: a knee injury. He was limited on Thursday. It's possible the Packers could return Chris Brooks this week, providing depth at running back if Lloyd can't go. Micah Parsons practiced in a limited capacity for the second straight day after returning on Wednesday. The Packers were in pads on Thursday. Parsons is not expected to play until Week 12 at the earliest. In addition to Nixon, the Packers did not have Zaire Franklin, Sean Rhyan, Travis Glover or Josh Whyle at Thursday's practice. All five are in danger of not playing against the Patriots. New England supposedly pursued the embattled wide receiver, who's apparently prepping to make a comeback following an extended absence from football. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Monday, Nov. 2 that Aiyuk is nearing a decision on new representation as he attempts to resume his playing career. The news comes with the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching and the Patriots dealing with injury-depleted receiving corps. San Francisco holds his rights and Aiyuk needs to file for reinstatement. However, the insider emphasized that Aiyuk can't swiftly join another organization. Via ESPN's Adam Schefter , Aiuyk has hired the legendary agent Drew Rosenhaus. San Francisco still controls his contractual rights, and the receiver must formally apply for reinstatement before he can resume his career. Aiyuk has remained on the reserve/left squad list since December 2025 following a breakdown in his relationship with the 49ers. His absence followed a four-year, $120 million extension signed in August 2024, although the 49ers subsequently voided approximately $27 million in guaranteed money for 2026. San Francisco general manager John Lynch previously indicated that the organization had no intention of bringing Aiyuk back. "It's safe to say he's played his last snap with the Niners," Lynch said in January . Before his injury, Aiyuk established himself as one of the league's more productive receivers, recording 75 receptions for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns during his All-Pro campaign in 2023.
