picks.blurb: Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:56 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Las Vegas Raiders arrive at Levi's Stadium with renewed confidence. The San Francisco 49ers arrive with extra rest and something to prove. Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a 38–33 victory over the Jets, improving to 4–4. San Francisco, meanwhile, returns from its bye at 6–1 after suffering its first defeat, a 29–20 loss to Atlanta. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brock Purdy throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Purdy will deliver his most convincing statistical statement of the season, reaching 350 passing yards and throwing four touchdown passes. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. home.blurb: All-Pro WR Brandon Aiyuk Will Return to 49ers: Report Just over a year after cutting off contact with the San Francisco 49ers , NFL All-Pro wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk will return to the team on Friday, according to a report from ESPN's Adam Schefter . 49ers' George Kittle Makes Feelings Clear on Brandon Aiyuk's Return 49ers Legend Steve Young Has Strong Words on Brandon Aiyuk's Return Unlock the latest Heavy on 49ers news — direct to your inbox. Well, this could be a little awkward. "Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has turned in paperwork to be reinstated, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus," Schefter wrote on his official X account on Wednesday. "Aiyuk, who currently is on San Francisco's Reserve/Left Squad list, will be reporting to the 49ers' training facility Friday afternoon, per Drew Rosenhaus. ‘Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,' Rosenhaus said. Once Brandon Aiyuk officially reports back to the 49ers, the organization's options are to keep him under his current contract, release him or potentially find a trade partner before Tuesday's deadline." Aiyuk hasn't played in over two years, since he suffered a catastrophic knee injury in Week 7 of the 2024 regular season — after the 49ers signed him to a 4-year, $120 million contract extension. The NFL trade deadline is November 10. "The move Brandon Aiyuk could've made months ago to force the 49ers ' hand," NFL Network's Mike Garafolo wrote on his official X account. "Now finally headed to the facility. Kyle Shanahan was asked in September if Aiyuk was an option and he said no. So this will seemingly result in Aiyuk's release." "49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk has filed for reinstatement and is prepared to report to the team's facility on Friday," The 33rd Team's Ari Meirov wrote on his official X account. " Once he does, San Francisco can't turn him away. The options are to keep him, cut him or somehow find a trade." Relationship Between Aiyuk, 49ers Disintegrated When he signed his contract extension, Aiyuk was coming off consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, including his only NFL All-Pro season in 2023, with 75 receptions for 1,342 yards and 7 touchdowns. Through 7 games in 2024, Aiyuk caught 25 passes for 374 yards and no touchdowns before a catastrophic knee injury in Week 7, when He tore his ACL and MCL against the Kansas City Chiefs . After Aiyuk cut off communications with the 49ers early in the 2025 season, the team chose to void the rest of the guaranteed money in Aiyuk's contract — approximately $25 million in salary for 2026. "We don't know what he's physically going to be like," Schefter said in March . "His knee was shredded." 49ers Desperate for Help at Wide Receiver While the 49ers have repeatedly said Aiyuk is no longer welcome on the team — mostly thanks to a series of social media tirades by Aiyuk — the sad part is that they desperately need help at wide receiver after injuries have decimate that position group. home.headline: 49ers’ George Kittle pleads the 5th on Brandon Aiyuk’s expected return to facility
home.blurb: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is reportedly inching closer to making a return to the NFL, after last having played in October 2024. Aiyuk suffered a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus injuries in his right knee against the Kansas City Chiefs, and now plans to return to the 49ers’ training facility. And well, tight end George Kittle hilariously declined to discuss Aiyuk’s potential return to the team, per a post on X by Grant Cohn. Kittle’s response came as Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, confirmed Wednesday that the 28-year-old had submitted the necessary paperwork to return and planned to report to the 49ers’ facility Friday afternoon. Rosenhaus said Aiyuk was healthy and ready to play, and San Francisco will now determine whether to reinstate Aiyuk. Related: Brandon Aiyuk’s agent confirms plan for return to 49ers facility “Plead the fifth, yeah. You can ask John. Or Kyle. Don’t ask me. I’m a conspiracy guy,” he said. General Manager John Lynch describing the situation as fluid and confirmed that the organization is working with the NFL Management Council to find a path that works for both sides, per ESPN. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said he had mentally moved on from Aiyuk and did not expect an immediate resolution. Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 season during his recovery. His relationship with San Francisco deteriorated further after the organization voided approximately $27 million in guaranteed contract money in July 2025, citing his failure to complete required rehabilitation sessions. The 49ers subsequently placed him on the reserve/left squad list in December after he stopped reporting to the facility, and his failure to report for training camp in July resulted in his placement on the reserve/did not report list. His current designation means San Francisco is not paying him and he does not occupy a spot on the active roster. The 49ers have previously attempted to trade Aiyuk, and a release remains a likely outcome. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. home.headline: Brandon Aiyuk files to make blockbuster 49ers return two years after last NFL game
home.blurb: Brandon Aiyuk files to make blockbuster 49ers return two years after last NFL game - The Mirror US Skip to main content The Mirror US - News, Sports, Celebrities and Showbiz News Over two years on from his severe knee injury, Brandon Aiyuk remains on the San Francisco 49ers reserve/did not report list - but he has applied to return to the active roster The return of Aiyuk is a stunning yet timely development. The former Second-Team All-Pro has applied for reinstatement and to make a stunning return to the NFL over two years after his last appearance in the league. The 6-1 49ers return to action against the 4-4 Las Vegas Raiders at Levi’s Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8. Aiyuk won’t be on the field, but he may be back in the NFL by then. Brandon Aiyuk has filed paperwork to be reinstated and intends to report to the San Francisco 49ers training facility. The 49ers are currently on a bye week after losing their first game of the season to the Atlanta Falcons. While the franchise stormed to the top of the NFC West with a 6-1 record through seven weeks, injuries have steadily built up, particularly on offense . “Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,” Drew Rosenhaus, who became Aiyuk’s agent on Monday, said on Wednesday. The 28-year-old - who is on San Francisco’s reserve/did not report list - intends to report to the 49ers' training facility later this week. Aiyuk has not played in the NFL since Oct. 20, 2024, when he tore the ACL, MCL, and meniscus in his right knee against the Kansas City Chiefs . However, his relationship with the 49ers has been up and down since. In July 2025, the 49ers voided approximately $27 million in guaranteed money on Aiyuk’s contract because the team deemed that the receiver did not do the requisite rehab sessions and check-ins during that offseason. When Aiyuk did not report for training camp, he was dropped to the reserve/did not report list. View 2 Images Brandon Aiyuk has returned to fitness and is looking to be activated (Image: Getty Images) Aiyuk has also been a trade target in the past. San Francisco tried to deal him, and the receiver implied on several occasions that he wanted to join the Washington Commanders to play alongside Jayden Daniels , the quarterback who threw him touchdowns at Arizona State. However, even if Aiyuk is reinstated, he will likely be dealt by the 49ers. Both 49ers general manager John Lynch and coach Kyle Shanahan have suggested Aiyuk’s time in the Bay Area is over, so a move could be made before the trade deadline on Tuesday. The Commanders may be an option, but the NFC East franchise has already signed veteran Stefon Diggs alongside other wideouts. It’s also unclear what kind of package Aiyuk would command given the length of his absence. The former first-round pick had emerged as one of the NFL’s most productive and exciting downfield receivers; Aiyuk tallied 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns in 2023.

away.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
away.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Main Navigation Search Search for: Weather Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published November 4, 2026 • Updated on November 4, 2026 at 3:15 pm Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Winners, losers as Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10 on Thursday Night Football Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy over debts from crash, alleged assault An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). away.blurb: If he were to return after the bye week, it would be on Dec. 20 at home against the New York Jets. Love was taken with the third pick in the 2026 NFL Draft in April and has been one of the most explosive players in the draft class. However, he has not been able to showcase much of that explosiveness in the NFL. The Arizona Cardinals have been dealing with a lot of changes on the offensive side of the football. After their ability to come back and defeat the Dallas Cowboys in overtime, they made the decision to switch starting quarterbacks. However, that is not going to be the only change for the offense, this time due to injury. Let’s take a closer look at who is injured and what it means for the Arizona Cardinals going forward. Arizona Cardinals are placing Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve ESPN’s Ian Rapoport is reporting that the Arizona Cardinals are placing star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve due to a high ankle sprain. This is obviously a major blow for the Cardinals, but they are well equipped to handle this type of injury with Tyler Allgeier coming off his best game of the season last week. Jeremiyah Love has been playing well this season as he has 76 rushing attempts for 268 yards (3.5 yards per carry) with a rushing touchdown and 11 receptions for 36 yards (3.3 yards per catch) with a receiving touchdown. Love was dealing with an ankle injury and missed two games due to it before returning on Sunday, but coach Mike LaFleur mentioned on Monday that this was a new injury. The initial diagnosis has Love missing 5-6 weeks, but he is guaranteed to miss the next four weeks, being placed on injured reserve. away.headline: Week 9 Injury Report: Cardinals at Seahawks
away.blurb: The Seahawks continued their week of preparation ahead of their Week 9 game against the Cardinals with a relatively long list of players not practicing. Given the short week coming off a Monday night game, it's entirely possible that some of the absences are precautionary, but it will be something to watch when the team puts out game statuses on Friday. Two players were new on the injury report, outside linebacker Derick Hall who did not practice due to a back injury, and linebacker Ernest Jones IV , who was limited with an ankle injury. Two players, outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and left guard link-placeholder-1 , went from limited Wednesday to not practicing on Thursday. Listed as non-participants for the second straight day were left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), quarterback Sam Darnold (quadricep/ribs), outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (foot), nose tackle Brandon Pili (back), receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger). For the Cardinals, guard Jon Gaines (ankle), running back Bam Knight (concussion) and tackle Jayden Williams (knee) were non-participants for the second day in a row. Cornerback Max Melton (knee) was new to the injury report with a knee injury, one of three players who were limited due to injury along with guard Isaiah Adams (ankle) and defensive tackle Walter Nolen (ankle). When Macdonald was asked about Williams on Wednesday, Macdonald said he, as well as Cross and Shaheed, "all have a chance to play. We haven't ruled anybody out yet." Among those listed as limited was quarterback Drew Lock , who is expected to start in Darnold's place. Lock has been dealing with an elbow injury that also had him limited the last two weeks and led to him serving as the emergency third quarterback behind Darnold and Jalen Milroe the past two games, as opposed to his usual role as the No. 2 quarterback. Also limited were guard Anthony Bradford (knee), running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring), guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle). For the Cardinals, guard Jon Gaines (ankle), running Bam Knight (concussion) and tackle Jayden Williams (knee) were non participants due to injury, while defensive tackle Walter Nolen (ankle) and guard Isaiah Adams (ankle) were limited. home.headline: Seahawks-Cardinals injury report: Leonard Williams held out with stinger, Drew Lock still limited
home.blurb: Seahawks-Cardinals injury report: Leonard Williams held out with stinger, Drew Lock still limited - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL The Seahawks had six players miss practice with injury, including quarterback Sam Darnold , left tackle Charles Cross and star defensive tackle Leonard Williams. "Big Cat" was held out with a stinger he suffered on Monday night against the Chicago Bears and would be a massive loss for the team, especially in the run game. Nose tackle Brandon Pili also did not practice with a back injury, leaving Seattle thin at the position and facing a red-hot running back in Tyler Allgeier. With Darnold out, Seahawks Mike Macdonald indicated that backup Drew Lock would start in his place . Lock has been battling an elbow injury for the last three weeks, was inactive in their last two games, and was once again limited in practice on Wednesday with a right elbow injury. If Lock can't go, second-year quarterback Jalen Milroe would need to step in to make his first NFL start, which would be as entertaining as it would be stressful. Sticking with the offense, newly acquired star guard Quenton Nelson was limited by a knee injury, as was backup Anthony Bradford. With Josh Jones poised to start another week at left tackle, more offensive line injuries have to be the last thing Seahawks fans want to see. While wide receiver Rashid Shaheed was held out of practice and appears on track to miss his second straight game, his backup Tory Horton was a full go with a hand injury. Take the good news where you can get it! The report proves to be a mixed bag for the Seahawks defense as well. Edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu, who missed last week, was limited with an ankle injury, and Nick Emmanwori was a full participant with a shoulder injury. Those two returning to form in the lineup would be a massive boost for the "Dark Side" defense that is reeling from giving up 34 points on Monday. As for the Cardinals, breakout wide receiver Michael Wilson was limited in practice by rest and a rib injury, which could give him a chance to play on Sunday. Wilson broke two ribs and put up 111 yards and a touchdown on eight catches in Arizona's win over the Dallas Cowboys last week. Defensive tackle Walter Nolen was also limited with an ankle injury. Arizona will likely be without running back Bam Knight, who would back up Allgeier, as he did not practice on Wednesday due to a concussion. The Cardinals held stars Budda Baker and Josh Sweat out of practice, but it was not injury-related. Humorously, the Cardinals held quarterback Jacoby Brissett out with "rest," which apparently means getting shipped off to the Baltimore Ravens . Tampa Bay just beat Atlanta 16–0 without completing a pass. Chicago comes in off an upset of Seattle. The Bears are 6-point favorites, and the total is 46.5. The Bucs have won three of their last four after an 0–4 start, so they are still in the NFC South race. These predictions lean on the contrast between Tampa Bay's run-first plan and Chicago's explosive offense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Caleb Williams leads the Bears past 30 points again Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Chicago will score at least 30 points, and Williams will account for three touchdowns. The Bears have scored 30 or more in every game Williams has finished this season, and they have not lost one he has started and finished (4–0). Since he returned from his hamstring injury, they have not trailed in any of three games. Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in a 30–24 win over New England. Chicago's pass offense averages 236.4 yards a game compared with 131.4 for Tampa Bay. That edge in the air is the core of this call. Tampa Bay's pass defense gives up 205.9 yards a game, which leaves room for chunk plays. Chicago's offense ranks 10th in EPA per play despite Williams missing three full games. I expect him to throw for at least 275 yards and add a rushing score. The one wrinkle is the Bears' backfield. Running back Kyle Monangai is listed as out with a thumb injury, which could shift more of the offense to Williams. Tampa Bay runs for 200 yards and still loses The Bucs will pile up another 200 rushing yards, and it still won't be enough. Against Atlanta, Tampa Bay ran 56 times for 324 yards. Bucky Irving gained 170 yards on 27 carries, and Kenny Gainwell added 140 on 25. Baker Mayfield attempted only three passes in steady rain. Chicago's run defense is beatable, allowing 4.4 yards per carry. Tampa Bay ranks eighth in EPA per rush, so the ground game will work on Sunday night. The problem is what happens when Chicago scores early. The Bucs average 22.3 points a game. A team rated poorly through the air can't easily come back against the best third-down defense in football, according to one projection. I'm projecting 200 rushing yards because the Bears' run defense can't stop everything. But Tampa Bay's offense needs scoring drives, not just yards, and the run game alone won't produce 30 points. Injuries make it harder. Gainwell is questionable with a hip issue, and outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was trending toward out. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was inactive last week with a foot injury and is also a concern. Mayfield throws 35 passes and the Bears win 34–20 The game ends with Chicago winning 34–20, and Mayfield forced into a very different afternoon than the one in Tampa. A 34–20 final would add up to 54 points, clearing the 46.5 total comfortably, and it would give Chicago a 14-point cover. Mayfield returned from a fractured thumb two games ago and is still working back to full rhythm. He has 679 passing yards and three touchdowns on the season, so asking him to throw 35 times is a real shift for this offense. That volume creates risk. If Chicago leads by two scores in the third quarter, Tampa Bay has to abandon the run and put the ball in Mayfield's hands. I expect two interceptions, including one that sets up a Chicago touchdown. The Bucs will compete. They'll move the ball, their kicker has been perfect this season and their defense will make a few plays. But the Bears' offense is more dangerous, and they are better built to play with a lead. This NFL season seems wide open. There isn't one great team yet and there are few trustworthy contenders who have emerged. The Bears seemingly saw it the same way when they traded two first-round picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. And through one game, it seems like a transformative trade. The Bears had a fantastic performance on a national stage, shutting down the Seahawks in a 34-17 win . Chicago's Super Bowl odds took a leap, as did Caleb Williams' MVP odds. In a season dying for a dominant team to emerge, maybe it's Chicago. The Bears' offense isn't a question. It has scored 30 points in every game Williams has started and finished (it did score just three points against the Vikings and Williams played three-and-a-half quarters, but that says something about Minnesota's defense). If Simmons has as big of an impact on the defense as it appeared on Monday night, Chicago will be looking really good. Nobody paying attention to the NFL hadn't seen how dominant Simmons is, but it was still impressive to see how quickly he fit in and made plays. Chicago gets another close-up in prime time this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night. Surprisingly, the Buccaneers are far better analytically than their 3-5 record would suggest. They're fifth in DVOA , eight spots ahead of the Bears, and eight in net EPA (expected points added) per play. The Bears are strong in net EPA, coming in third. The Buccaneers will be completely overshadowed in this game. The Bears will be the focus on Sunday night as they've emerged as one of the NFL's most dangerous teams. That's a reason they're a healthy 6.5-point favorite. That's a lot of points, and the Buccaneers might be secretly pretty good. That's why Buccaneers +6.5 is the pick. And if the Bears blow out Tampa Bay in a big prime-time window, they'll take over as the talk of the NFL, if they're not already. The Bears are 4-0 in games that Caleb Williams started and finished this season. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 9 of the NFL season: Jaguars (-10) over Ravens Even at -10, the line seems too low. The Jaguars have three wins by 24 points or more and two came against the 5-3 Browns and the 5-3 Patriots. They're good. There could be a letdown facing Baltimore undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano, and it's possible the Ravens rally around Fagnano for a season-saving performance with Jacoby Brissett on the way next week. But this seems like a huge ask for the Ravens, who have scored 13 or fewer points in three straight games. Bengals (-3) over Falcons The Bengals and Falcons go to Madrid, Spain, for this one. The Falcons are nearly impossible to figure out. They followed up a win over the undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a pass. That sums up Atlanta's season. We should trust Joe Burrow, who is on a heater, though there are more questions about Cincinnati's defense after it gave up 36 points to the Titans at home last week. Giants (-3) over Eagles Maybe Joe Milton III gives Philadelphia a boost and the Eagles get their first win since Week 2. But since Jalen Hurts went on IR, the Eagles have lost all three games by double digits. It's not a good team in any way, and Milton is far from a sure thing. The Giants are off a bye and should be feeling good coming into this one. Panthers (+2.5) over Broncos The Broncos are the better team. A few things work against them in this spot: It's an early start on the East Coast, and the Panthers have three days rest advantage. The Broncos are also coming off an emotional win over the Chiefs and there could be a letdown. Denver has been much better at home this season. Carolina has faded after a good start but this is a decent opportunity for a win. Dolphins (+7) over Lions Give Miami credit for playing hard. Maybe at some point that effort starts to fade, but the last time they truly got blown out was Week 2. They lost by 14 points to the Chiefs, but Kansas City led by only seven points with three minutes left. It's possible the Lions score enough to cover, but remember that they're usually a different team outdoors. Chiefs (-10) over Jets Kansas City will enjoy the breather after facing the Seattle and Denver defenses on the road the past two weeks. This seems like the type of game in which the Chiefs could take out their frustrations on an opponent that does have some talent but has won only once since Week 1. Saints (-3) over Browns The Browns are likely going with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback because Deshaun Watson was put in concussion protocol. It's not like Watson was playing so well he's irreplaceable, but Sanders has thrown only three passes all season. The Saints are well rested coming off a bye. The Saints are not a great team this season, but this might be a spot for them to get right. Rams (-5.5) over Commanders Is it time to trust the Rams? They have covered two games in a row without a sweat. Those wins came against mediocre (Raiders) or bad (Chargers) teams, but they did handle business. And the Commanders are mediocre at best and maybe just bad. Let's see if the Rams are truly back. Cowboys (-5.5) over Colts It is incredibly hard to trust the Cowboys, especially as a road favorite. But what we saw from the Colts last week in a 42-7 loss was troubling. There was no fight left in that team, which has lost key players to trades and knows its season is done. This could be a bad mistake, trusting a defense that can't stop anyone to cover almost a touchdown on the road. Taking the Colts at this point is even harder. Texans (-4.5) over Chargers It's a lot for Houston to be favored by this much on the road, however, home-field advantage has been mostly eliminated this NFL season and the Chargers have no home-field advantage — even if that was still a thing. Houston is coming off a bye and still has hopes to revive its season. The Texans still have a 34.4% chance to make the playoffs according to DVOA. The Chargers are 0.0% on that list. They'll cover a spread at some point but it's hard to anticipate when it happens. Raiders (+10) over 49ers The Raiders have four losses, and they came against four of the better teams in the NFL: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. The bad news is this week they get the Super Bowl favorites. The 49ers should be getting many players back after their bye. But the Raiders can move the ball and they're getting a lot of points. Seahawks (-8.5) over Cardinals With all the quarterback chaos this week, we get two teams that had a different quarterback in Week 8. Brissett was benched and traded, and Gardner Minshew II takes over. Sam Darnold has a quad injury and he'll be out, with Drew Lock taking over. Lock is a reasonable replacement, and Minshew isn't facing the Cowboys defense this week. Packers (+3) over Patriots The Patriots have a lot of injuries and the Packers have a few days of extra rest. In a game that seems evenly matched, the small edges add up. Green Bay started the season very slow but has looked much better over the last four games, winning three and barely losing at Detroit. New England has also emerged after an early-season slump to win four of five. This is a really fun matchup, and even enough to feel OK taking the points. Vikings (+3.5) over Bills This is an interesting game because the teams have opposite strengths. The Bills have a great offense and bad defense, and the Vikings have a bad offense and great defense. The Minnesota defense held the Bears to three points after all; Chicago has scored 30 points in every other Caleb Williams start. It will be a great test against Josh Allen, who is having another fantastic season. It's never enjoyable to be going against Allen, but getting 3.5 points with a defense this good seems right … as long as the offense does at least a little bit. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sam Householder · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears return to Soldier Field to cap off a hat trick of primetime games. They're hoping to finish the three-game stretch at 3-0 as they head into their bye week, but a tough Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad stands in the way. Chicago is riding high after back-to-back wins over last season's Super Bowl participants, but the Bucs should not be overlooked. Will the Bears fall victim to a trap spot or will Ben Johnson continue to keep the team focused and not let them buy into the hype the media has built up around them? For Tampa Bay, it's a chance to shake off their 0-4 start and prove their improvements over the last month weren't a fluke. The Bucs come in having won three of their last four games and the only loss came in overtime. Their defense ranks first in the league. However, the offense has been clunky. Over the last two weeks, they've won resoundingly with virtually no passing game (in last week's 16-0 win, no "virtually" modifier was needed). Dive into the Bucs and what it will take for the Bears to remain on a winning streak. Tampa Bay Buccaneers SB Nation site: Bucs Nation Record: 3-5, second in the NFC South Last week: 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons Game day, time, TV: Sunday, 7:20 p.m. CT, NBC Sunday Night Football Spread: Bears -6.5 Bears all-time record against: 40-22 Historical meetings: Week 10 of the 2001 season. The Bears defense held the Bucs' offense in check in the first half, allowing only three Tampa field goals. Jim Miller and Marty Booker had their connection going though. They connected for three touchdowns –28-, 44- and 66-yards. A late comeback by the Bucs gave the Bears a scare. Brad Johnson rushed for a 1-yard score and hit Mike Alstott for a 2-point conversion with 2:29 left in the game. Chicago ended up punting back to Tampa but Johnson was picked off by Tony Parrish. Anthony Thomas fumbled, giving the Bucs new life. Johnson hit Warrick Dunn along the sideline but R.W. McQuarters was flagged for unnecessary roughness, giving them another 15 yards. That allowed Tampa to attempt a 48-yard field goal, but they missed it as time expired. The Bears won 27-24. Last meeting: Week 2 of 2023. The Bears offense had its moments, but the defense was shredded. Mike Evans had 171 yards and a touchdown, while Baker Mayfield threw for 317 yards. Justin Fields threw for 211 yards and rushed for a TD. However, he threw two interceptions. DJ Moore had 104 receiving yards. Chase Claypool also had a touchdown. A late pick-six by Shaquil Barrett off Fields sealed a 27-17 Bucs win. Injury report: The Bucs listed five players on their injury report. Limited participation RB Kenny Gainwell (hip) S Tykee Smith (ankle) Did not participate OLB Yaya Diably (knee) WR Emeka Egbuka (foot) DL Elijah Roberts (personal) Offense: The Buccaneers come into Chicago ranked 20th in points and 25th in yards. Their passing offense ranks 29th, while their rushing offense ranks first. Quite the disparity, but the numbers are backed by the past two weeks when they've passed for a total of 62 yards. Baker Mayfield (61.8 pct cmp./679 yds./3 TD/2 INT) missed three games with a thumb injury that he's now playing through. However, he has done minimal passing since returning and Tampa's numbers reflect that. Emeka Egbuka (28 rec./240 yds./2 TD) is the leading receiver for the Bucs, but he's been injured. Chris Godwin (27/243/0), Cade Otton (19/186/0) and the running backs Bucky Irbing (18/78/1) and Kenneth Gainwell (12/61/1) are the other receiving leaders for Tampa. Tez Johnson (9/178/1) and Ted Hurst (11/168/1) have also caught some passes. On the ground, however, Irving (148 att./728 yds./5 TD) and Gainwell (58/289/0) are getting the production for the Bucs. They're each averaging 5.0 yards per carry. In fact, every Tampa player with a rushing attempt is averaging at least 5 yards per carry. Defense: Tampa's defense comes in ranked fifth in points and third in yards allowed. They rank eighth in passing defense and second in rushing defense. The dominant unit is led by LBs Josiah Trotter (68 tkls/1 INT/3 PD/1 sk/3 TFL/1 QB hits) and Alex Anzalone (42 tkls/3 INT/1 sk/2 TFL/1 QB hits/3 PD). S Tykee Smith (1 INT/43 tkls/3 TFL/4 QB hits/2 PD) is also making plays all over. Up front, OLBs David Walker (4 sk/6 TFL/6 QB hits), YaYa Diaby (3 sk/6 TFL/6 QB hits/2 PD/1 INT) and Al-Quadin Muhammad (2 sk/1 FF/1 PD/4 QB hits/2 TFL) are getting after opposing QBs. Veteran A'Shawn Robinson (1 sk/2 INT/3 PD/1 TFL/2 QB hits) is playing well. In the secondary, Jacob Parrish (2 INT/13 PD/3 TFL) leads the league in pass breakups. Zyon McCollum (30 tkls/2 INT/9 PD/1 TFL) and Keionte Scott (39 tkls/4 PD/1 sk/1 QB hit) are making plays, too. Key matchups: It's a classic battle of the trenches. The Bears OL needs to best Tampa's DL to establish the run and allow Caleb Williams to use play action to take downfield shots. Keeping Williams clean will allow the offense to be at its best. On defense, the Bears need to slow Irving and Gainwell down and not allow them to chew up the clock and get easy yards. Forcing Baker into passing situations and play from behind benefits the Bears. The Bucs have allowed more than 300 yards of offense only three times this year. They beat the Cowboys 24-16 but lost to the Cincinnati Bengals (33-27) and Pittsburgh Steelers (26-19 in OT). The Bears have had less than 300 yards of offense in their two losses. Baker Mayfield has 14 pass attempts and 64 passing yards in the past two games. He's completed only half of his attempts. The Bucs defense is tied for the best DADOT at 6.6. Their pressure percentage is fifth-worst at 19.3 percent, despite having the seventh-highest blitz percentage at 33.6 percent. Tampa's pass defense is really good. Opposing QBs have a 74.9 rating against them and just 205.9 yards per game. Can the Bears finish off their trifecta of primetime games against top defenses undefeated? Is this a trap spot for Chicago?

away.headline: Buccaneers week 9 injury report: Egbuka returns to full practice
away.blurb: According to the Buccaneers' official injury report , Egbuka returned to full practice after missing Wednesday with a foot injury. The second-year receiver has missed Tampa Bay's last two games, making his return a positive development for an offense that has totaled just 64 passing yards during that stretch. Quarterback Baker Mayfield practiced fully for the second consecutive day despite his right thumb injury. Running back Kenneth Gainwell improved from limited to full participation with a hip injury, while safety Tykee Smith remained limited with an ankle injury. Chris Godwin and Bucky Irving did not practice because of veteran rest days. Defensive lineman Elijah Roberts returned to full participation after missing Wednesday for personal reasons. Chicago also has a few players dealing with injuries, including running back Kyle Monangai, who has missed consecutive practices with thumb and toe injuries. Defensive tackle Grady Jarrett and offensive tackle Theo Benedet improved to limited participation Thursday after missing Wednesday. DNP = Did not participate. Full = Full participation. Limited = Limited participation. A dash indicates the player was not listed that day. Chicago held a walkthrough Wednesday, so its participation report is an estimate. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers received encouraging news Thursday as wide receiver Emeka Egbuka returned to full practice, while outside linebacker Yaya Diaby and left tackle Tristan Wirfs did not participate ahead of Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Chicago Bears . Diaby missed practice for the second consecutive day with a knee injury suffered against Atlanta in Week 8. He played just seven defensive snaps before exiting the game. NFL Network previously reported that Diaby suffered a Grade 2 MCL sprain, putting his availability against Chicago in doubt. Wirfs was another notable absence Thursday, appearing on the report with a toe injury after not being listed Wednesday. His participation Friday will be worth monitoring ahead of Tampa Bay's matchup with Chicago's defensive front. home.headline: Bears Add Earnest Brown IV After Kentavius Street Injury Leaves DT Depth Thin
home.blurb: The injury bug bit the Chicago Bears hard this week. Early on Wednesday afternoon, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune reported that left tackle Braxton Jones will miss the rest of the season following surgery on his knee. Jones was placed on Injured Reserve (IR) on October 3 with the hope that he could return later in the season, but those hopes have been dashed. Just hours after Jones' injury update, more injury news followed. The Bears announced that they had placed defensive tackle Kentavius Street on IR, and head coach Ben Johnson later said that it was "unlikely" that he would return this season, according to a report from Brad Biggs . This leaves the Bears dangerously thin along the defensive line, as Dayo Odeyingbo also remains on IR. While Street is far from Chicago's top defender, they'll feel his loss. Street had been a dependable contributor to Dennis Allen's defense, earning a solid 70.6 impact grade from Pro Football Network. In training camp, Street had impressed Dennis Allen even more than rookie Jordan van den Berg , who had become a fan-favorite for his tenacious style of play. Of course, the NFL is a 'next man up' league, and this rash of injuries to Chicago's defensive line opens the door for rookies to play a larger role than they previously had. Jordan van den Berg in particular stands to gain quite a bit should he see more snaps against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9. Plus, the Bears now know that they can simply lean on superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons after he dismantled the Seattle Seahawks in the Bears' statement primetime victory on Monday. Bears make roster moves to address season-ending injuries In light of these season-ending injuries to Street and Cole Kmet, the Bears made two roster moves on Wednesday to add to their depth. They signed tight end Stephen Carlson from the practice squad to the active roster, then added defensive tackle Earnest Brown IV to the practice squad, according to Brad Biggs . Brown, a fifth-round pick in the 2021 NFL draft, has appeared in 15 regular season games between stints with the L.A. Rams and Buccaneers. In case the Bears continue to lose defensive tackles, he can step in and handle a small role, given his experience. As for Carlson, he's been with the Bears since 2023 but has only appeared in four regular season games, most recently against the Seahawks. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Two 6-1 teams enter Monday Night Football with very different questions. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. picks.headline: Bills at Vikings: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 9 game
picks.blurb: Two 6-1 teams, one marquee matchup. The Bills visit Minnesota after beating the Ravens 36-10, while the Vikings look to rebound from their first loss, a 19-15 defeat in Detroit. Kyler Murray's hamstring is the biggest injury to watch. Kevin O'Connell said Murray remained under evaluation Monday. Carson Wentz is the next option if Murray cannot play but, even if he starts, his mobility deserves attention. Wentz guided the Vikings to wins over the Packers and Bears in September, completing 59% of his passes with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Minnesota's protection is another concern. Left tackle Christian Darrisaw is dealing with shoulder soreness. His availability becomes especially important if Murray's hamstring limits his ability to escape pressure. Josh Allen's supporting cast needs monitoring, too. Joshua Palmer injured his hamstring against Baltimore, DJ Moore picked up another injury concern, and right tackle Spencer Brown missed that game with a back issue. Their practice participation will matter this week. The early market favors Buffalo on the road. The Bills are favorites of -3/-3.5 points, depending on where you do your shopping, and the total has dropped from 48.5 at open to as low as 45.5. Murray's status could move both numbers. If you're curious to read a couple of interesting trends: The Vikings are a perfect 7-0 SU and ATS in the fourth quarter this season, while the Bills are 6-0-1 SU and 7-0 ATS in the second quarter. These aren't shocking stats when you consider the teams are a combined 12-2 on the year, but just thought we'd pass it along. Vikings vs Bills odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Bills -3.5 Moneyline: Bills -170; Vikings +155 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Vikings vs Bills USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Bills 24, Vikings 20 Do we have a Super Bowl preview on our hands? Guess that depends how you feel about Minnesota's offense and Buffalo's defense. Either way, we've got a pair of 6-1 teams, a few superstar talents in Josh Allen, James Cook and Justin Jefferson, plus a banged up Kyler Murray with a hamstring injury that could move the line before kickoff. Whether it's Murray or Carson Wentz stepping in for him again, I still trust the Bills more to manufacture points. Brian Flores and the Vikings defense will make Allen work for everything – as the Lions just experienced in their low-scoring win – but the visitors simply have more at their disposal and I like them to remain unbeaten on the road. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Bills 21, Vikings 14 For a team that was the league's last undefeated group standing, the Vikings are facing quite a bit of strife. A rickety offense might soon become fully broken if Kyler Murray continues to miss on downfield opportunities. Jim Leonhard's defense has hardly been a bunch of world-beaters, but the opportunistic group continues to come up with big plays in key moments, particularly with its pass rush. If the Bills can get Murray off schedule, it could be a difficult evening for Minnesota. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Vikings 21, Bills 16 Offense or defense? Like Week 8, the Vikings find themselves in a matchup that features strength vs. strength and weakness vs. weakness. It was the Lions offense that triumphed against the Vikings defense, but there's reason to believe things could be different this week. Buffalo has been much looser with the football this year, turning it over 11 times – which ranks 11th-most in the league, while Detroit has the third-fewest. Suddenly, you see the Vikings' path to victory. Brian Flores' defense forces Josh Allen into a mistake or two on Monday night and that is the difference. away.blurb: Minnesota's odds in this game have dropped quite a bit with Murray's injury, and it's possible they could move further if he sits out in Week 9. Sports Illustrated spoke to oddsmakers about the injury a,d BetMGM's Christian Cipollini, a Senior Trading Manager, explained that the spread would move quite a bit if Wentz gets the start. For now, bettors and fans have to wait and see if Murray is able to log at least a limited session in Thursday's practice. Based on the latest odds movement, he seems to be 50/50 for Monday's showdown with Josh Allen and the Bills. Kyler Murray Injury Update: NFL Insider Casts Doubt on Vikings QB's Status; Odds vs. Bills Shift Skip to main content ON SI Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is up in the air for Week 9 against the Buffalo Bills due to a hamstring injury that he suffered in the team's Week 8 loss to the Detroit Lions. Earlier this week, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed that Murray is dealing with a hamstring issue and that he'd be re-evaluated this week. Murray and the Vikings don't play until Monday night in Week 9, so they have yet to release a practice report since their first official session will come on Thursday. That has left the quarterback's status in limbo with the Vikings (6-1) looking to remain in the top spot in the NFC North. NFL insider Ian Rapoport doesn't believe that Murray is dealing with a long-term injury, but he did mention that Murray may not play since he's a mobile quarterback and can't move around as well. That would pave the way for veteran Carson Wentz to get the start, something he did in place of Murray in Week 2. "If it is Wentz this line will probably close around Bills -6. There's no doubt that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as an upgrade over Wentz. This season, Murray has completed 64.9 percent of his passes for 1,022 yards, five scores and three picks while adding 29 carries for 167 yards on the ground. The Vikings are in the bottom three in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on offense, so Wentz doesn't have a high bar to clear if he's the quarterback on Monday night. home.headline: Vikings Announce Carson Wentz Decision Amid Kyler Murray Injury and Struggles
home.blurb: Wentz's numbers from his limited playing time earlier this season whilst Murray was in concussion protocol far exceed what the former first overall pick has managed to accomplish since taking back the reins. Vikings Announce Carson Wentz Decision Amid Kyler Murray Injury and Struggles Unlock the latest Heavy on Vikings news — direct to your inbox. The Minnesota Vikings have been accused of preparing a "soft benching" for struggling quarterback Kyler Murray for much of this past week as the former Arizona Cardinal deals with a hamstring injury. Having yet to announce an injury report, considering that they play on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills , head coach Kevin O'Connell had not given much concreted indication as to what Murray's practice or playing status might look like over the coming days. However, speaking to the media on Thursday, O'Connell revealed that Murray's injury will force him to miss Monday's game, and that Carson Wentz will start instead. " The #Vikings are planning to start Carson Wentz on MNF against the #Bills , as Kyler Murray's hamstring injury would limit his mobility. Murray also could make it worse by playing." Ian Rapoport reported on Thursday. Is This a Soft Benching for Kyler Murray? The Super Bowl champion from 2018 has a passer rating 20 points higher than Murray, averages 0.44 more yards per throw, and has a far better touchdown to interception ratio (3:0 v.s. 5:3). Minnesota have a gruelling three-game schedule against the Bills, Packers and 49ers over the next three weeks, and whilst the injury may simply be a coincidence, it could also be that O'Connell knows he will need his best at the helm in order to remain contenders to top the NFC North and the conference as a whole. home.blurb: "How Are They Going to Trust Her?": Linda Cohn Raises Major Doubts About Dianna Russini's Return Months After Mike Vrabel Scandal “Kyler Murray Just Wants to Play More Call of Duty”: NFL Fans React as Vikings QB Loses Starting Job to Carson Wentz - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' What MLB's labor proposal means Carson Wentz © Instagram/cj_wentz11 Andrés Linares · College Sports Network Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:08 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Carson Wentz is slated to play for the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night as they clash with the Buffalo Bills. This comes as Kyler Murray was revealed by the team to be dealing with a hamstring injury. Murray arrived in Minnesota this season after seven seasons with the Arizona Cardinals. Wentz has been with the Minnesota Vikings since last season, when he started five games as J.J. McCarthy battled injuries. Fans reacted to the news on X, joking about the fact that Kyler Murray is a well-known video game fan. "Nah Kyler just wants to play more cod (Call of Duty)," one fan wrote . Should J.J. McCarthy have stayed at Minnesota? Some fans expressed regret that the Vikings had recently parted ways with the former Michigan signal-caller. What a roller coaster of a career for Carson Wentz. Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell on his decision to start Carson Wentz On Thursday, Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell made public his decision to start Carson Wentz over Kyler Murray against the Buffalo Bills. "After evaluating Kyler on Monday, getting some imagery and things, we did determine he does have a hamstring strain," O'Connell said . "We don't believe it to be more than a week-to-week kind of thing right now, but for him, his movement skills and the way he plays the game, we do feel like we'd be putting him at risk of possibly turning this into a more significant injury than it is by trying to have him work through it here early on. "Obviously there's a ton of confidence in Carson," O'Connell added. "He's already helped us — had a major role in two wins this year against two really good teams. He's a steady presence and a guy we know."
